<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_010"></a>
## CORE-010: Token Immutability

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_010` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `e5baab372e4f3277`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| A token is an immutable value object consisting of a typed payload value and a creation timestamp.<br><br>Once created, neither the value nor the timestamp can be modified.<br><br>*When* a transition fires and nothing else changes the marking between the firing's consumption and its deposit, every token a place holds after the firing *shall* be a token the place held before the firing, with the same value and creation timestamp, or a token the action emitted to that place, and the firing *shall* not duplicate any of these tokens.<br><br>*When* a transition fires and nothing else changes the marking between the firing's consumption and its deposit, every token that a place without a reset arc of the transition held before the firing *shall* still be in that place after the firing, with the same value and creation timestamp, unless the action received it from that place as a consumed input.<br><br>*When* a transition fires, every token its action receives from one of its input places or read places *shall* be a token that place held before the firing, with the same value and creation timestamp, and the action *shall* not receive a consumed token more often than its input place held it. | 1. For every transition t with no input arc and read arc on one place (ruling D15), every firing of t from M that delivers δ, emits e and leaves M':<br>2. every place p ends holding a sub-multiset of its tokens in M followed by the tokens e sends to p;<br>3. every place p that is neither an input place nor a reset place of t still holds every token it held in M, with multiplicity;<br>4. every input place p of t that is not a reset place holds every token it held in M, with multiplicity, apart from the tokens δ delivers as consumed from p;<br>5. the tokens δ delivers as consumed from an input place p are a sub-multiset of the tokens p held in M;<br>6. every token δ delivers as read from a read place p is a token p held in M. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>    NoInputRead t →<br>      (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦<br>            ∀ (p : N), (M' p).Subperm (M p ++ EmittedTo e p)) ∧<br>        (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>            on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦<br>              ∀ p ∉ inPlaces t, ¬ResetArc t p → (M p).Subperm (M' p)) ∧<br>          (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>              on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦<br>                ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t, ¬ResetArc t p → (M p).Subperm (δ.inputs p ++ M' p)) ∧<br>            (∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>                on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦<br>                  ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t, (δ.inputs p).Subperm (M p)) ∧<br>              ∀ (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>                on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M x ↦<br>                  ∀ (p : N), ReadArc t p → ∀ x ∈ δ.reads p, x ∈ M p</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is one step Q t M δ e M' (glossary: QFireRel): t fires from the queue marking M, delivers δ to its action (the consumed tokens per input place and the read tokens per read place), the action emits e (places and tokens, in emission order) and the firing leaves M'. T is the token itself, its value and its creation timestamp together, so 'the same value and creation timestamp' is equality in T, 'a token the place held' is membership in the place's queue and 'duplicate' or 'more often' compares occurrence counts (List.Subperm: every token occurs at most as often on the left as on the right).
- The firing is atomic, as one step of Q is: the first two EARS sentences are scoped to a firing with nothing else changing the marking between its consumption and its deposit. In all three runtimes an asynchronous action's outputs are deposited when its completion is processed, in a later cycle than the consumption (Java BitmapNetExecutor fireTransition and its completion handler; Rust and TypeScript alike), and other firings and injected tokens can change the marking in between, so after such a firing a place need not hold the tokens it held when the firing consumed. The third EARS sentence is local to the consumption and needs no scope. The same property for interleaved firings (each firing takes the head of its input places when it starts and appends at the tail when it completes) is stated locally by EXEC-010 and EXEC-020; over the executor cycle it is the companion of the executor model (RefExec, W5).
- The first quoted sentence is the definition the statement is read against: a token is its value and its creation timestamp, compared by content (a value object), which is equality in T. The 'typed payload' (a value of the place's token type) is CORE-001's and IO-006's subject and is not encoded; T is one abstract type for every place.
- The second quoted sentence is read at the engine seam, as the three EARS sentences restate it: the engine never rewrites, drops or copies a token it holds or moves. The same property at other seams belongs to their IDs: a Forward keeps the consumed token's value and timestamp (IO-014 AC5, below RefQFire), a restore keeps both (CORE-073 AC1), and tokens an action publishes before it completes (IO-015) are deposited outside a single firing (RefExec, Phase 2). An action or user code mutating a token object, deep immutability of the payload (a Java record holding a mutable object, a Rust Arc<T> with interior mutability) and runtime freezing in TypeScript are API shape (AC3), not claimed here.
- e is the emission of a completion the executor processed and output validation accepted ([EXEC-020], [EXEC-021], ruling D17); a discarded, timed-out, stopped or failed completion is not a step of Q. The tokens of e are new tokens the action created, so the block says nothing about their values or timestamps (CORE-011's subject). Because e is a parameter of the step, line 1 alone accepts a relation that re-stamps a place's tokens and lists the new copies in e; lines 2 and 3 kill it whatever e lists, since the original tokens must still be there (CORE_010_forbids_launder).
- Every line is stated for transitions satisfying NoInputRead (ruling D15): a transition with an input arc and a read arc on one place is rejected when it is built (EXEC-012) and never fires, so the EARS sentences, which carry no such premise, say nothing more than the lines about any transition that can fire. The reference meets the lines without that premise too; the premise is there so that the block is exactly a corollary of the signed EXEC blocks, which carry it.
- Derived: under D15, the lines follow from EXEC-020 (every place keeps a base followed by its emitted tokens; a place without an input arc and a reset arc keeps its queue as base, an input place that is not a reset place a sublist of it), EXEC-013 line 1 (a reset place holds exactly its emitted tokens), EXEC-010 line 1 (an input place that is not a reset place ends as a permutation of its queue after the consumed prefix followed by its emitted tokens), EXEC-010 line 2 (the delivered inputs are the FIFO prefix) and EXEC-012 line 1 (every read token is the head of the place), by CORE_010_of_EXEC. Every relation the forbids theorems here reject is therefore also rejected by one of those blocks; the block adds the link from the CORE-010 prose, not a new constraint.
- Line 1 is the first EARS sentence. A firing that re-stamps the tokens a place keeps onto pairs the place did not hold is killed by it (CORE_010_forbids_restamp; lines 2 and 3 kill it too). A firing that keeps every token and adds one more copy of a kept token is killed by line 1 alone (CORE_010_forbids_dup): lines 2 and 3 ask only that the held tokens stay, so its 'shall not duplicate' half is line 1's, and a reading of line 1 by membership accepts the copy (CORE_010_mutant_line1Membership_killed_dup). Order is not compared: that the kept tokens are the queue after the consumed prefix, in order, is EXEC-010's and EXEC-020's.
- Lines 2 and 3 are the second EARS sentence, split by whether the place is an input place, so that δ.inputs is consulted only where t has an input arc. They catch a rewrite that line 1 cannot see because the new token equals another held or emitted token: unit tokens (CORE-012) whose value ring and timestamp ring run out of step (CORE_010_forbids_desync, line 3), a place that stamps every token with its last arrival so that a held token becomes a copy of the emitted one (CORE_010_forbids_lastArrival, line 2), and the laundering relation above (CORE_010_forbids_launder, line 2).
- Lines 4 and 5 are the third EARS sentence, split by arc kind: line 4 for input places, line 5 for read places. An altered copy handed over as an input (CORE_010_forbids_alteredInput) or as a read (CORE_010_forbids_alteredRead) is killed, and so is an action that receives the head token k times for an exactly(k) input (CORE_010_forbids_headTwice, line 4). Line 5 is membership only: a read arc delivers the head once per arc, so a place read by two arcs legitimately hands over one token twice (qReadsBag); the read multiplicity is EXEC-012's. Both lines are restricted to the input places and the read places of t: what an action receives from a place that is neither is not constrained here, as in EXEC-010 and EXEC-013, because the spec has no shall sentence on it.
- 'neither the value nor the timestamp': a reading under which only the value is immutable accepts a firing that keeps every value and re-stamps the kept tokens; CORE-010 kills it (CORE_010_mutant_valueOnly_killed). A reading by membership instead of multiplicity accepts the laundering, desync, last-arrival and head-twice relations; CORE-010 kills each (CORE_010_mutant_membership_killed_*).
- Like most on … shall lines, the lines hold of the relation that takes no step; the coverage conjunct QCovers Q F of the queue consistency theorem rules that out (exec020_empty_not_covers).
- AC1 (token value accessible after creation and matching the original) is read at the engine seam as lines 1 to 5: a token the action receives, or a place keeps, is the token as created, value included (CORE_010_nonvacuous: the action receives (10, 0) and (20, 3), place 0 keeps (11, 1) and (12, 2), place 2 keeps (40, 5)). The accessor itself is API shape, checked by tests, not encoded.
- AC2 (token timestamp accessible after creation) is API shape: an accessor exists in every language with a token object. It is checked by tests and not encoded; that the timestamp a kept or delivered token carries is its original one is lines 1 to 5.
- AC3 (no API to mutate token fields after creation) is API shape (kind Q in the plan): checked by tests and by each language's type system, not encoded. Whether the API-shape criteria bind the Python binding, which has no token object, is open ruling D99 and is not relied on.
- The test derivation (create a token with value 42, its value is 42 and its timestamp is set) is AC1 and AC2 and is not encoded.

The `ToString` instance only names the build check of EXEC-012 and does not occur in CORE-010.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_013"></a>
## CORE-013: Token FIFO Ordering

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_013` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `afc8627e912fddc4`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens within a place are stored in FIFO (first-in, first-out) order.<br><br>The oldest token is consumed first when a transition fires.<br><br>*When* a transition fires and nothing else changes the marking between the firing's consumption and its deposit, each place that is neither one of its input places nor one of its reset places ([CORE-034]) *shall* end the firing holding its whole queue from before the firing, in queue order, followed by the tokens the firing deposited there, in the order the action produced them ([EXEC-020]).<br><br>*When* a transition fires and nothing else changes the marking between the firing's consumption and its deposit, its action *shall* receive from each input place that is not a correlated input of its match specification ([NU-020]) the first tokens of the place's queue before the firing, in queue order; unless the place is also one of its reset places, the place *shall* end the firing holding the rest of that queue, in queue order, followed by the tokens the firing deposited there, in the order the action produced them ([EXEC-010], [EXEC-020]). | 1. For every queue firing relation Q:<br>2. for every firing of a transition t and every place p that is neither an input place nor a reset place of t: the queue p holds after the firing is the queue it held before the firing, followed by the tokens the action emitted to p, in emission order;<br>3. for every firing of a transition t and every input place p of t: there is a number k such that the tokens delivered to the action from p are the first k tokens of p's queue before the firing, in queue order, and, if p is not a reset place of t, the queue p holds after the firing is the queue it held before without those k tokens, followed by the tokens the action emitted to p, in emission order. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>      ∀ p ∉ inPlaces t,<br>        ¬ResetArc t p →<br>          on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦ M' p = M p ++ EmittedTo e p) ∧<br>    ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>      ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,<br>        on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦<br>          ∃ k,<br>            δ.inputs p = OldestFirst M p k ∧<br>              (¬ResetArc t p → M' p = List.drop k (M p) ++ EmittedTo e p)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing relates a queue marking before it to the queue marking after it, with what it delivered to the action and the emissions of the action (glossary: Queue order, QueueMarking, Delivered, QFireRel, Emitted to). 'Oldest' is read as the glossary's Queue order defines it: the oldest token is the head of the place, the one added first (OldestFirst, Head). It is not the token with the smallest timestamp (created_at): a token can carry a stamp older than a token added before it (a host-supplied stamp, CORE-011; a restore, CORE-073), and an executor that keeps each place sorted by stamp is forbidden (CORE_013_forbids_stampOrder). The rewording of the word 'oldest' in NU-020 that clash K8 proposes waits for ruling D20 and is not relied on here.
- The firing is atomic, as one step of Q is: both shall sentences are scoped to a firing with nothing else changing the marking between its consumption and its deposit. In all three runtimes an asynchronous action's outputs are deposited when its completion is processed, in a later cycle than the consumption (Java BitmapNetExecutor fireTransition and its completion handler; Rust and TypeScript alike), and other firings and injected tokens can change the place in between: if t, asynchronous, deposits into p while a synchronous u consumes p's head before t completes, p does not end holding its whole queue from before t's firing. The same order for interleaved firings (each firing takes the head when it starts and appends at the tail when it completes) is stated locally by EXEC-010 and EXEC-020; over the executor cycle it is the companion of the executor model (RefExec, W5).
- Correlated inputs (ruling D16, clash K7): the second shall sentence excludes a correlated input of a ν-net match specification, as EXEC-010 does. The first needs no exclusion: every place a match names is a declared input (NU-020), and the first sentence speaks only of places that are not input places. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every input place is one that is not a correlated input, and line 2 quantifies over every input place. How a correlated input consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here; this block makes no claim about it. The model's scope is what keeps correlated inputs out of line 2 today, and the holds theorem is the check that it still does: if the model gains match specifications and the reference consumes a correlated input by name, line 2 fails at a correlated input whose matched tokens are not the head of its queue, CORE_013_reference (through EXEC_010_reference) can no longer be proved, and the exclusion must then be written into line 2.
- The prose sentence 'The oldest token is consumed first when a transition fires.' carries no exception in its own words; it is read through the second shall sentence, which carries D16's. Adding the exception to that prose sentence and to the other count-level sentences is ruling D30, still open: until it is ruled, the section holds two normative sentences that disagree on correlated inputs, and the block relies on neither outcome.
- Line 1 is the first shall sentence and the prose sentence 'Tokens within a place are stored in FIFO (first-in, first-out) order.', as far as one firing can show it: a place the firing neither consumes from nor resets keeps every token it held, in queue order, and gains tokens only at the tail, in the order the action produced them. That such a place loses nothing is also EXEC-020's second line and CORE-035's count line; line 1 states it so that the first shall sentence cannot be read as letting a firing take head tokens from a read, inhibitor, output or untouched place. Input places are line 2's. A reset place is left out: it ends the firing holding exactly what was deposited there (CORE-034, EXEC-013). Line 1 kills an executor that deposits at the head of the queue (CORE_013_forbids_headDeposit), an executor whose read arcs pop the head of a read place (CORE_013_forbids_readPop), a bag reading that keeps the right tokens in any order (CORE_013_mutant_bag_killed), and the weaker reading that lets every place that is not a reset place lose some of its first tokens (CORE_013_mutant_headLoss_killed).
- Line 2 is the second shall sentence and the prose sentence 'The oldest token is consumed first when a transition fires.': the action receives the first tokens of each input place, in queue order, and on an input place that is not a reset place the place keeps the rest of its queue, followed by the emitted tokens in emission order, since the same k fixes the delivery and the removal. How many tokens leave (k) is the consumption count of the input arc (EXEC-010, IO-007, CORE-030), not repeated here. On an input place that is also a reset place only the delivery half applies; the place is drained (CORE-034). Line 2 says nothing about what is delivered from a place that is not an input place, as EXEC-010 and EXEC_013.lean leave it open; an action that receives tokens from such a place is ruled out by CORE-060 AC4 and CORE-063, which have no block yet. Delivering the oldest tokens newest first is killed by line 2 (CORE_013_forbids_reversed), and so is a stack reading (CORE_013_mutant_lifo_killed).
- The block is derived: core013_of_EXEC proves it of every relation that satisfies EXEC-010 and EXEC-020 (line 1 is EXEC-020's first two lines on a place that is neither an input nor a reset place), so it adds no constraint of its own at the grain of one firing, and its holds theorem is EXEC_010_reference and EXEC_020_reference composed. It is kept as a block because CORE-013 is the requirement the other IDs cite for queue order (EXEC-010, CORE-073, MOD-021).
- Order across the phases of the executor (tokens injected through an environment place, the initial marking, tokens deposited earlier in the same firing pass, and a restore, CORE-073 AC6) needs the executor model (RefExec, wave W5) and is deferred to it. Tokens an action published before it completed (IO-015) are not modelled: the action emits only at the end of the atomic firing (ruling D17).
- AC1 (tokens A, B, C added in order, consuming one yields A) and AC2 (consuming again yields B) are checked on the reference by CORE_013_nonvacuous, with tokens 10, 11, 12 for A, B, C added one after another to place 0 of the empty marking (and 40 to place 2): the first firing of a One input on place 0 delivers 10 and leaves 11, 12 on place 0 and 40, 30 on the output place 2; the second delivers 11 and leaves 12. The statement gives only the consuming half of the two criteria, and only up to the count: under it alone a firing may deliver any prefix of the queue, and that a One input takes exactly one token is EXEC-010's count line (with IO-007 and CORE-030). The adding half (a token added outside a firing goes at the tail, so A, B, C added in order are held as A, B, C) is CORE-070's add line, which rejects a store that adds at the head; CORE_013_nonvacuous builds its marking with the reference add (qAppend) and does not test it. Adding through an environment place or a restore, across the executor's phases, is RefExec's (W5).
- The test derivation (add three tokens, remove them one at a time, check FIFO order) is the same check as AC1 and AC2. Adding a token outside a firing is CORE-070's add line, and removing one outside a firing is CORE-070's removeFirst (removeFirst_fst: it returns the head); CORE_070_nonvacuous runs the adds and a removal on the reference.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_022"></a>
## CORE-022: Transition enablement

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_022` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `85f3b6c51be85f72`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| A transition is **enabled** in a marking when every input place holds at least its required count (see [IO-001]–[IO-004]), every read place is marked and no inhibitor place is marked.<br><br>*While* an input place of a transition holds fewer tokens than its required count, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a read place of a transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* an inhibitor place of a transition is marked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a transition is enabled, the transition *shall* be able to fire.<br><br>This requirement concerns transitions that build. A definition that building the transition rejects ([CORE-030], [IO-002], [IO-004], [EXEC-012], [IO-011]–[IO-014]) is not a transition of any net and is never enabled anywhere; in particular an output spec whose alternatives no write can tell apart ([IO-012]) never reaches a marking. | 1. For every transition t that builds (Builds t: at most one input arc per place, every input arc requiring at least one token, no place with both an input arc and a read arc, no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every forward's from an input place, no two output branches claiming the same set of places):<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which the place of some input arc of t holds fewer tokens than that arc's required count;<br>3. t does not fire from a marking in which some read place of t is unmarked;<br>4. t does not fire from a marking in which some inhibitor place of t is marked;<br>5. from every marking m in which t is enabled, t fires to some marking m'. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>    Builds t →<br>      (while fun m ↦ ∃ s ∈ t.core.inputs, m s.place &lt; requiredCount s.card, never<br>          Fire F t) ∧<br>        (while fun m ↦ ∃ p, ReadArc t p ∧ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>          (while fun m ↦ ∃ p, InhibitorArc t p ∧ Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>            ∀ (m : CountMarking N), Enabled t m → ∃ m', Fire F t m m'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Enabled' is the glossary term (`Enabled`, readable form `enabled_iff`); 'can fire' / 'able to fire' is read as 'some firing exists'. The last line says a firing exists, not that an executor performs it now: when an enabled transition actually fires is the subject of the timing and scheduling requirements (TIME-*, EXEC-*).
- Enablement is a function of the current marking alone: the three 'shall not' lines forbid a firing from every marking in which a condition fails, whatever happened before. This is how 'when any condition ceases to hold, the transition becomes disabled' of the previous wording is read.
- The input condition ranges over every input arc of t, not only the first one per place. Under CORE-030 a transition has at most one input arc per place, so the two readings coincide on every transition that can be built.
- The 'able to fire' line needs every transition to have at least one way to end (an output branch, or the empty deposit when it has no output spec); the reference semantics has one for every output spec (`Reference.exists_deposit`).
- Transitions with a ν match specification (NU-020) add a correlation condition on top of these three; this block reads CORE-022 for transitions without one, as the reference semantics has none.
- The inhibitor line restates the first clause of CORE-031 because CORE-022 lists it as one of its conditions; it is kept so that this block stands on its own.
- 'Transitions that build' is read as the build-time checks themselves (`Builds`): the input-arc check of CORE-030, the input-count checks of IO-002 and IO-004 (no Exactly(0), no AtLeast(0)), the input-and-read check of EXEC-012 (ruling D15) and the output-spec checks of IO-011 (a place twice in one branch), IO-013 (more than one Timeout node), IO-014 (a ForwardInput outside a Timeout child; a forward from a non-input place) and IO-012 (two output branches claiming the same set of places). A transition that fails one constrains nothing here: no executor ever holds it, so it neither fires nor is required to. Branch sets are compared as sets (`SameSet`), so Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B)) and Xor(And(P, A), And(P, B)) build and are covered, while Xor(P, P) and Xor(And(A, B), And(B, A)) are not.
- The reference `Out` is binary; n-ary And / Xor are read as right-nested, which keeps the IO-016 enumeration order, so the IO-012 branch indices and the build verdict are those of the n-ary spec.
- AC1 (satisfied inputs, reads present, inhibitors empty, enabled) is the last line.
- AC2 (missing input tokens, disabled) is the second line.
- AC3 (missing read tokens, disabled) is the third line.
- AC4 (inhibitor place has tokens, disabled) is the fourth line.

This is the relation that also satisfies IO-012, whose `Xor(Place(0), Place(0))` transition (`core022_dup`) does not build.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_022 CORE_022_refFireBuilt</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_030"></a>
## CORE-030: Input arc

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `291c542b00432099`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume from each of its input places that is not also one of its reset places ([CORE-034]) as many tokens as the input arc's consumption count ([IO-001]–[IO-004], [IO-007]), oldest first.<br><br>*When* a transition fires, each of its input places that is neither one of its reset places nor one of its output places *shall* end the firing holding exactly the consumption count of its input arc fewer tokens than it held before the firing. | 1. For every transition t that declares at most one input arc per place, every input place p of t whose input arc has cardinality c, p not a reset place of t, and every deposit d, every firing of t from m to m' depositing d, from a marking in which p holds at least the arc's required count:<br>2. leaves m'(p) + consumptionCount(c, m(p)) = m(p) + (the tokens d deposits in p): the firing removes exactly the consumption count from p, besides what it deposits there;<br>3. and, if p is not an output place of t either, leaves m'(p) + consumptionCount(c, m(p)) = m(p): p ends holding exactly the consumption count fewer tokens, whatever deposit the firing reports. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (c : Card),<br>    InputPlacesDistinct t →<br>      InputArc t p c →<br>        ¬ResetArc t p →<br>          ∀ (d : List N),<br>            on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>              requiredCount c ≤ TokenCount m p →<br>                TokenCount m' p + consumptionCount c (TokenCount m p) =<br>                    TokenCount m p + Deposits d p ∧<br>                  (¬OutputArc t p →<br>                    TokenCount m' p + consumptionCount c (TokenCount m p) =<br>                      TokenCount m p)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. Markings are token counts (glossary: Marking).
- AC1 (a transition with an input arc consumes tokens from the place on firing) is the second line, with the amount the consumption count of the arc's cardinality; the third line is the second quoted sentence.
- AC2 (consumed tokens follow FIFO order) and 'oldest first' are not encoded: which tokens leave a place is below the token-count granularity of the firing relation.
- AC3 and the sentence 'If a transition declares two input arcs on the same place, building the transition shall fail with a descriptive error that names the transition and the place and suggests a single arc with `exactly(n)` / `atLeast(n)` instead.' are not encoded: the firing model has no transition builder and no error values. They are read as a hypothesis instead: the requirement constrains only transitions whose input places are distinct (InputPlacesDistinct), the only ones AC3 lets any executor, state-class graph or verifier see. Firings of a transition with duplicate input arcs are left unconstrained here, as the spec says their consumption has no coherent semantics.
- The build-time output-spec checks (IO-011 to IO-014) are not a hypothesis here: neither line depends on the output spec beyond which places it names, so both hold of every transition with distinct input places, whether or not its output spec builds.
- A place that is both an input place and a reset place of t is excluded by both quoted sentences: CORE-034 says such a place ends the firing holding exactly what was deposited there, so it is CORE-034's to constrain (the third hypothesis, ¬ ResetArc t p).
- Interpretation: the consumption is read additively, m'(p) + consumed = m(p) + deposited, so a firing that also deposits into its own input place is counted correctly.
- The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count on a place the output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc): no firing of t can deposit there ([CORE-035]), so the consumption shows in the marking alone, as the third line says. Without it a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit equal to the consumption count in its input place would pass the second line. This is the guard IO-001 to IO-004 also carry, so each of those blocks stands alone.
- Interpretation: both lines are required only of firings from a marking in which p holds at least the arc's required count. A firing from a marking where p holds fewer is not enabled (CORE-022, IO-005); whether such a firing may happen at all is those requirements' business, and CORE-030, which speaks only of how much a firing consumes, says nothing about it.
- 'The same place' is equality of place names (TypeScript, Rust, [CORE-002]); Java's name-and-type equality is not modelled.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_030): The reference semantics satisfies CORE-030: `Seam.fireNC` leaves a non-reset place with `m p - nconsumed + deposited`, `Seam.nconsumed` is the consumption count of the arc `nspecAt` finds, and enablement (`Seam.enabledNA`) guarantees the place holds at least the required count, so the subtraction does not truncate. A reference firing deposits only in places its output spec names, so outside them the deposit is empty and the place loses exactly the consumption count.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_030 RefFire</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030_allows_unenabled` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_030): CORE-030 allows a firing of a transition that is not enabled, as long as every enabled firing consumes the consumption count: the unguarded firing relation satisfies CORE-030, and `core030_t .one` firing from an empty place `0` tells it apart from the unguarded mutant, which would forbid that firing although CORE-030 says nothing about it.
  <pre>CORE_030 core030_unguardedFire ∧ ¬CORE_030_mutant_unguarded core030_unguardedFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030_forbids_ghost` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_030): ✗ A firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit in its input place violates CORE-030 (third line): `core030_t .one` has no output place, fires from one token in place `0`, reports a deposit of one token there, and leaves that token in place `0`.
  <pre>¬CORE_030 core030_ghostFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030_forbids_idle` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_030): ✗ A firing that consumes nothing through its input arcs violates CORE-030 (second line): `core030_t .one` fires from one token in place `0` and leaves that token there.
  <pre>¬CORE_030 core030_idleFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030_mutant_noConsume_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_030): The idle firing kills the no-consumption mutant: it satisfies it (nothing changes, nothing is deposited) but not CORE-030.
  <pre>CORE_030_mutant_noConsume core030_idleFire ∧ ¬CORE_030 core030_idleFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030_mutant_required_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_030): The required-count firing kills the second mutant: it satisfies it, but `core030_t .all` fires from two tokens in place `0` and leaves one, where CORE-030 says `All` consumes both.
  <pre>CORE_030_mutant_required core030_requiredFire ∧ ¬CORE_030 core030_requiredFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030_mutant_trustDeposit_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_030): The ghost-deposit firing kills the trust-deposit mutant: the deposit it reports in each input place makes up for the tokens it does not take, so it satisfies the mutant; but `core030_t .one` has no output place, and its input place keeps its token.
  <pre>CORE_030_mutant_trustDeposit core030_ghostFire ∧ ¬CORE_030 core030_ghostFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_030_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_030): Both lines of CORE-030 are exercised by the reference semantics: `core030_t .all` has a single input arc, of cardinality `All`, on place `0`, which is neither a reset place nor an output place, and it fires from two tokens in place `0` to none, consuming both.
  <pre>InputPlacesDistinct (core030_t Card.all) ∧<br>  InputArc (core030_t Card.all) 0 Card.all ∧<br>    ¬ResetArc (core030_t Card.all) 0 ∧<br>      ¬OutputArc (core030_t Card.all) 0 ∧<br>        RefFire (core030_t Card.all) (core030_at0 2) [] (core030_at0 0)</pre>
- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.spec_consistent_coreIO` (Libpetri.Spec.Consistency): ✓ The CORE and IO requirement blocks hold together: the reference builder, the reference firing relation and its timed-out firings satisfy every behaviour block, and the reference ambiguity check, consumption contract, output validator and branch enumeration satisfy IO-012, IO-007, IO-015 and IO-016.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_031"></a>
## CORE-031: Inhibitor arc

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_031` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `4f884470bf67c07e`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* an inhibitor place of a transition is marked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* an inhibitor place of a transition is unmarked, the inhibitor arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire. | 1. For every transition t and every inhibitor place p of t:<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which p is marked;<br>3. from a marking m in which p is unmarked, t fires to m' exactly when t without its inhibitor arcs on p fires from m to m'. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>    InhibitorArc t p →<br>      (while fun m ↦ Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        ∀ (m : CountMarking N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>          ¬Marked m p → (Fire F t m m' ↔ Fire F (withoutInhibitor t p) m m')</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists'.
- AC1 (inhibitor place empty, enablement unaffected) is the second line: with p unmarked, removing the inhibitor arcs on p changes neither whether t fires nor where it leads.
- AC2 (inhibitor place marked, transition disabled) is the first line.
- AC3, first half (a firing consumes nothing through its inhibitor arcs): by the second line a firing of t from a marking with p unmarked is a firing of t without its arcs on p, so those arcs add nothing to what it consumes or produces; by the first line t does not fire when p is marked. AC3, second half: what a firing of another transition consumes through an input arc on p is CORE-030's subject, not this block's.

**Evidence**

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_032"></a>
## CORE-032: Read Arc

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `114ece4e82239077`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a read place of a transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a read place of a transition is marked, the read arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire or the marking its firing leaves.<br><br>*When* a transition fires, each of its read places on which it has neither an input arc nor a reset arc *shall* end the firing with its token count before the firing plus the tokens the firing deposits there. | 1. For every transition t and every read place p of t:<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;<br>3. from a marking m in which p is marked, t fires to m' exactly when t without its read arcs on p fires from m to m';<br>4. if t has no input arc and no reset arc on p, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) = m(p) + (tokens d puts in p). | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>    ReadArc t p →<br>      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (∀ (m : CountMarking N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>            Marked m p → (Fire F t m m' ↔ Fire F (withoutRead t p) m m')) ∧<br>          ((∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) →<br>            ¬ResetArc t p →<br>              ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>                F t m d m' → m' p = m p + Deposits d p)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists'.
- AC1 (read place must have tokens for enablement) is the second line.
- AC2 (token remains in place after firing) is the fourth line, for a read place the transition neither consumes from nor resets. A place that is also an input place or a reset place of the same transition loses tokens through those arcs ([CORE-030], [CORE-034], [EXEC-013] AC4); the third line says the read arc adds nothing to that loss.
- AC3 (action receives the read token value) is not encoded: the firing relation works on token counts and has no action or token values. Which token is read is [EXEC-012]'s subject, the context access [CORE-061]'s.
- 'Marked' is read as 'holds at least one token' (glossary: Marked), the spec's 'at least one token for enablement'.
- AC2's 'token remains' is encoded at count level only. A firing that takes the read token out of p and puts it, or another token, back in the same step leaves the same counts and satisfies this statement, but moves the token to the FIFO tail and changes its timestamp. Token identity, FIFO position and timestamp are below the count granularity of the firing relation, as for CORE-030 AC2; they belong to [EXEC-012] ('both A and B remain after firing', the oldest is peeked), and no count-level block can catch the bug.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): The reference semantics satisfies CORE-032: `Seam.enabledNA` requires every read place to hold a token, so `t` does not fire while `p` is unmarked; the consumption (`Seam.nconsumed`), the deposits and the effect (`Seam.fireNC`) never read the read arcs, so with `p` marked removing them changes nothing; and with no input arc and no reset arc on `p`, `Seam.fireNC` leaves `m p - 0 + Deposits d p` there.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_032 RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_forbids_ignoresRead` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): ✗ Ignoring the read arc violates CORE-032 (first clause): `core032_t` fires from the empty marking.
  <pre>¬CORE_032 core032_ignoresReadFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_forbids_readAlwaysBlocks` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): ✗ A read arc that blocks its transition while its place is marked violates CORE-032 (second clause): `core032_t` cannot fire from the marked marking, but without its read arc it can.
  <pre>¬CORE_032 core032_readAlwaysBlocksFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_forbids_readConsumes` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): ✗ Consuming the read token violates CORE-032 (third clause): `core032_t` fires from the marking with one token in every place and leaves place `0` empty, depositing nothing.
  <pre>¬CORE_032 core032_readConsumesFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_forbids_skipReadReset` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): ✗ Skipping the reset of a read place violates CORE-032 (second clause): with one token in place `0`, `core032_tRes` without its read arc fires and drains place `0`, but no firing of `core032_tRes` leaves place `0` empty.
  <pre>¬CORE_032 core032_skipReadResetFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_mutant_dropConserve_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): The clearing firing kills the third mutant: it satisfies the mutant (it fires exactly when the reference does, and the reference satisfies the first two clauses) but not CORE-032 (`core032_t` fires from the marked marking and leaves place `0` empty, depositing nothing).
  <pre>CORE_032_mutant_dropConserve core032_clearsAllFire ∧ ¬CORE_032 core032_clearsAllFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_mutant_dropMarked_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): The always-blocking firing kills the second mutant: it satisfies the mutant (a transition with a read arc never fires) but not CORE-032 (`core032_t` does not fire from the marked marking although it fires there without its read arc).
  <pre>CORE_032_mutant_dropMarked core032_readAlwaysBlocksFire ∧<br>  ¬CORE_032 core032_readAlwaysBlocksFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_mutant_dropUnmarked_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): The idle firing kills the first mutant: it satisfies the mutant (whether a transition fires does not depend on its arcs, and no firing changes a token count) but not CORE-032 (`core032_t` fires while its read place is unmarked).
  <pre>CORE_032_mutant_dropUnmarked core032_idleFire ∧ ¬CORE_032 core032_idleFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): All three clauses of CORE-032 are exercised by the reference semantics: `core032_t` has a read arc on place `0` and no input or reset arc there; it does not fire from the empty marking, although without its read arc it does (first clause); it fires from the marked marking, as it does without its read arc (second clause); and that firing deposits nothing and leaves place `0` holding its one token (third clause).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_033"></a>
## CORE-033: Read arc multi-reader

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `a864c7bea1b325a9`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a place is marked, a read arc to that place *shall not* stop its transition from firing, so all transitions with read arcs to the place can be enabled simultaneously.<br><br>*When* a transition with a read arc to a marked place fires, and the transition has no input arc and no reset arc to that place, the read arc of any transition to that place *shall not* stop that transition from firing afterwards (no conflict), since read arcs do not consume tokens. | 1. For every transition t and every read place p of t, at every marking m in which p is marked:<br>2. if t without its read arcs on p can fire from m, then t can fire from m;<br>3. for every two transitions t₁, t₂ with read arcs on p, where t₁ has no input arc and no reset arc on p:<br>4. after every firing of t₁ from a marking m in which p is marked to m', if t₂ without its read arcs on p can fire from m', then t₂ can fire from m'. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>      ReadArc t p →<br>        ∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>          Marked m p →<br>            (∃ m', Fire F (core033_withoutRead t p) m m') → ∃ m', Fire F t m m') ∧<br>    ∀ (t₁ t₂ : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>      ReadArc t₁ p →<br>        ReadArc t₂ p →<br>          (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t₁ p c) →<br>            ¬ResetArc t₁ p →<br>              on Fire F t₁, shall fun m m' ↦<br>                Marked m p →<br>                  (∃ m'', Fire F (core033_withoutRead t₂ p) m' m'') →<br>                    ∃ m'', Fire F t₂ m' m''</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking.
- AC1 (two readers both enabled when the place has tokens) is the first two lines: whether a firing relation lets t fire from m depends on t and m alone, so 'both enabled' is each enabled, and each reader's read arc on a marked p adds no condition. The text does not claim a reader fires with its other arcs unsatisfied, hence the comparison with the reader without its read arcs on p.
- AC2 (both can fire without conflict) is read in the untimed interleaving: firing one reader does not take away, through p, the other reader's ability to fire (last two lines). Conflicts through other places (t₁ consuming an input of t₂, or depositing into an inhibitor place of t₂) are not this block's subject.
- The restriction to a t₁ with no input arc and no reset arc on p is an interpretation choice: such a t₁ removes tokens from p (CORE-030, CORE-034; EXEC-012 allows a read arc and a reset arc on one place), so it can disable the other reader; the text's reason 'read arcs do not consume tokens' covers the read arcs only.
- t₁ and t₂ may be the same transition: a reader firing twice in a row is covered too. In the untimed step model this is no stronger than the case of two transitions with the same arcs.
- The read token's value reaching the action (CORE-032 AC3, EXEC-012) is below the count granularity and not this block's subject.
- Both clauses assume p is marked: a reader firing from an empty read place is CORE-032 AC1 (its first clause), not this block's subject. A firing relation that ignores read arcs satisfies this block (CORE_033_allows_ignoresRead).
- Clause 2 asks only that p stay marked for the other reader, which is what 'no conflict' needs. That a read leaves the count of p unchanged (apart from deposits) is CORE-032 AC2 (its third clause); the 'since read arcs do not consume tokens' of this text is that requirement's reason, not a second acceptance criterion here. A read that takes one token whenever two or more are present satisfies this block (CORE_033_allows_readTakesSurplus).
- Each firing is one atomic step, so a read token held or reserved while the reader's action runs (taken at the start and put back at completion, or a per-place lock on read places), which would keep two readers from being in flight together, cannot be expressed here. In-flight concurrency of readers needs a start/complete step model (CONC, EXEC); a take-and-put read that reorders the FIFO queue is below count granularity (EXEC-012).

CORE-032's first clause rejects it (CORE-032's `CORE_032_forbids_ignoresRead`, for the same relation).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_034"></a>
## CORE-034: Reset arc

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `93e6155b06c813c7`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires, each of its reset places *shall* lose every token it held before the firing and end the firing holding exactly the tokens the firing deposited there.<br><br>A reset arc *shall not* affect whether its transition can fire, whether the reset place is marked or not.<br><br>A reset arc *shall not* change what its transition can deposit: from every marking, the transition and the same transition without its reset arcs *shall* be able to make exactly the same deposits, so a reset arc neither adds a deposit nor removes one.<br><br>A reset arc *shall not* change the token count of any place other than its own. | 1. For every transition t and every reset place p of t, writing t∖p for t without its reset arcs on p:<br>2. every firing of t that deposits d leaves p with exactly as many tokens as d puts in p, whatever p held before;<br>3. every firing of t∖p from a marking m that deposits d is matched by a firing of t from m whose deposit puts the same number of tokens in every place (a reset arc removes no deposit, and t fires wherever t∖p does);<br>4. every firing of t from m that deposits d is matched by a firing of t∖p from m whose deposit puts the same number of tokens in every place and that leaves every place other than p with the same token count (a reset arc adds no deposit, t∖p fires wherever t does, and the arc changes no other place). | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>    ResetArc t p →<br>      (∀ (d : List N),<br>          on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧<br>        (∀ (d : List N),<br>            on fun m m'' ↦ F (withoutReset t p) m d m'', shall fun m x ↦<br>              ∃ d' m', F t m d' m' ∧ SamePerPlace d d') ∧<br>          ∀ (d : List N),<br>            on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>              ∃ d' m'',<br>                F (withoutReset t p) m d' m'' ∧<br>                  SamePerPlace d d' ∧<br>                    ∀ (q : N), q ≠ p → TokenCount m' q = TokenCount m'' q</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking: removing a reset arc changes where a firing leads, so the second sentence compares the existence of a firing, not its target. It is the existence half of the second and third lines taken together (`CORE_034_canFire`), so it has no line of its own.
- Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place are the same deposit, whatever their order (`SamePerPlace`).
- AC1 (fires even if the reset place is empty) is the second line at a marking with p empty: the reset arc on p adds no condition, so t fires there whenever t∖p does. The text does not claim t fires with its other arcs unsatisfied.
- AC2 (all tokens removed on firing) is the first line. A reset place that is also an output place keeps what the firing deposited there (glossary: Deposit); a reset place that is also an input place ends with the deposit too, whatever was consumed from it.
- AC3 (no token requirement, no contribution to enablement) is the second and third lines at every marking, empty or marked.
- AC4 (same deposits with and without the reset arc, compared per place; a reset arc on an output place neither adds nor removes an outcome) is the second line (no outcome removed) and the third line (no outcome added).
- The third line is also the frame of a reset arc: it rules out a reset that also empties a place the transition has no arc to, and a reset whose removed tokens feed a Forward or timeout deposit (they are not consumed; IO-013/IO-014 forward only consumed tokens). It compares against the same transition without the arc rather than spelling out the whole marking change; the effect of the other arcs is CORE-030, CORE-031, CORE-032 and IO-013's subject.
- The comparison is over firing relations, not over which output specs build: a transition and the same transition without its reset arcs have the same output spec, so the build-time checks of IO-011 to IO-014 accept both or neither.
- Token counts only: which tokens are removed, and EXEC-003 AC5 (a reset later in the same firing pass leaves same-pass deposits in place) are below this granularity; that refinement is EXEC-003's subject, not this block's.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): The reference semantics satisfies CORE-034: `Seam.fireNC` sets a reset place to the deposit count (`refFire_apply`), neither `Seam.enabledNA` nor the deposit (`Seam.nconsumed`) reads the reset arcs, so a firing of `t` and of `t` without its reset arcs on `p` exist at the same markings with the same deposits, and `Seam.fireNC` reads the reset arcs only at the reset place itself.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_034 RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_firstBranch` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset arc that removes a deposit violates CORE-034 (second clause): without its reset arc `core034_tXor12` deposits in place `2`, with it only in place `1`.
  <pre>¬CORE_034 core034_firstBranchFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_keepsTokens` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset arc that removes nothing violates CORE-034 (first clause): under the idle firing `core034_t` fires from `core034_full`, deposits nothing, and place `0` keeps its three tokens.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_resetAfterDeposit` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset that also removes the firing's own deposit violates CORE-034 (first clause): `core034_tOut` deposits one token in its reset place `0` and must end holding it, not zero.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_resetNeedsToken` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset arc with a token requirement violates CORE-034 (second clause): without its reset arc `core034_t` fires from the empty marking, with it no firing matches.

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_mutant_dropFrame_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): The neighbour-emptying firing kills the third mutant: the reset place itself ends with the deposit and every firing without the arc is matched by one with it (the mutant holds), but place `1` is emptied by a reset on place `0` (CORE-034 fails).

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_mutant_dropRemoves_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): The first-branch firing kills the second mutant: its firings are reference firings, so they empty every reset place and are matched by the firing without the arc (the mutant holds; a deposit of the first branch stays one when a reset arc is dropped, because the deposit does not read the reset arcs), but `core034_tXor12` cannot deposit in place `2` although it can without its reset arc (CORE-034 fails).

- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): All three clauses of CORE-034 are exercised by the reference semantics: `core034_t` has a reset arc on place `0`; from `core034_full` it fires and empties place `0` (first clause, three tokens removed, none deposited), where without its reset arc place `0` would keep them, while every other place ends the same with and without the arc (third clause); it fires from the empty marking, as it does without its reset arc (second clause, reset place unmarked); `core034_tOut`, whose reset place is also its output place, ends with place `0` holding the one token it deposited there (first clause with a nonzero deposit); and `core034_tXor` (AC4), with the reset arc on one of its two output places, deposits in place `0` or in place `1` exactly as it does without the arc, and after depositing in place `0` holds that token alone there.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_035"></a>
## CORE-035: Output arc

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `7ce7e918319b593c`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires, it *shall* deposit tokens only in its output places, according to its output spec (see [IO-010]–[IO-015]).<br><br>*When* a transition fires, the marking the firing leaves *shall* hold every token the firing deposited.<br><br>*When* a transition fires, every place that is neither an input place nor a reset place of the transition *shall* change by exactly the tokens the firing deposited there. | 1. For every transition t and every deposit d:<br>2. every firing of t that deposits d puts tokens only in places that t's output spec names;<br>3. every firing of t that deposits d leaves a marking in which every place holds at least as many tokens as d put there;<br>4. every firing of t that deposits d, from m to m', leaves every place p with no input arc and no reset arc of t holding m p plus what d put in p, no more and no less. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N),<br>    (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦<br>        ∀ (p : N), Produced d p → OutputArc t p) ∧<br>      (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ ∀ (p : N), Deposits d p ≤ m' p) ∧<br>        on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>          ∀ (p : N),<br>            (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) → ¬ResetArc t p → m' p = m p + Deposits d p</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. 'When the transition's action completes' is read as 'when the firing deposits', for every outcome: the timeout outcome ([IO-013]) also deposits only in places the output spec names (a Timeout child, a ForwardInput's `to`).
- An output place is a place the transition's output spec names (glossary: Output arc), every Xor branch, Timeout child and ForwardInput `to` included. A transition with no output spec has no output place, so its firings deposit nothing.
- Which output places one firing deposits in, and how many tokens, is the subject of [IO-010]–[IO-016] ('according to its output spec'), not of this block: a firing relation that never deposits satisfies CORE-035 and is ruled out by [IO-016].
- The second line says only that the deposited tokens are in the resulting marking; the exact count of an input place is [CORE-030]'s and of a reset place [CORE-034]'s. A reset place that is also an output place ends holding exactly what was deposited, which satisfies the line.
- The third line is the marking side of 'only in its output places': on every place [CORE-030] and [CORE-034] do not cover (a pure output place, a read-only or inhibitor-only place, a place with no arc), the firing adds exactly its deposit. A place the firing does not deposit in is therefore unchanged, and an output place keeps its earlier tokens (no overwrite, no double or deduplicated deposit). On read places this coincides with [CORE-032]'s third clause.
- AC1 (after the transition fires, produced tokens appear in the output place) is the second line, with the first saying the place is an output place.
- AC2 (output tokens carry the current timestamp): not encoded. The firing relation works on token counts and carries no token timestamps; timestamps are [CORE-011] and the timed semantics' subject.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): The reference semantics satisfies CORE-035: `Reference.deposit` takes its tokens from an output branch (`Out.branches`) or from the first `Timeout` child (`Out.timeoutDeposits`), both of which name only places of the output spec; and `Seam.fireNC` adds the deposit's counts to every place (after consumption, or in place of the old count on a reset place), so a place with no input or reset arc gains exactly the deposit.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_035 RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_dedup` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ A deduplicating store violates CORE-035 (third clause): `core035_t` fires from `core035_one`, and place `0` keeps one token instead of two.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_dedupFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_double` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ A double deposit violates CORE-035 (third clause): `core035_t` fires from the empty marking and place `0` ends with two tokens for a deposit of one.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_doubleFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_lost` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ Losing the deposited tokens violates CORE-035 (second clause): `core035_t` deposits a token in place `0`, but under `core035_lostFire` the marking it leaves is still empty.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_lostFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_overwrite` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ Overwriting an output place violates CORE-035 (third clause): `core035_t` fires from `core035_one`, and place `0` ends with one token instead of two.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_overwriteFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_phantom` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ A phantom write violates CORE-035 (third clause): `core035_t` deposits only in place `0`, yet place `7` gains a token.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_phantomFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_resetAfter` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ Resetting after depositing violates CORE-035 (second clause): `core035_r` deposits a token in its reset place `0`, which `core035_resetAfterFire` then empties.

  <pre>CORE_035_mutant_dropOutputs core035_strayFire ∧ ¬CORE_035 core035_strayFire</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_036"></a>
## CORE-036: Arc semantics summary

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_036` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors; the outcome line with output validation enabled (CONC-026, the default) · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `78d3fa5e658ee902`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* an input place of the transition holds fewer tokens than the required count of its input arc, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a read place of the transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* an inhibitor place of the transition is marked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* the transition is enabled, it *shall* be able to fire, whatever its output places and reset places hold.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each input place that is not a reset place *shall* lose the consumption count of its input arc, and gain what the firing deposits there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each place that is neither an input place nor a reset place *shall* lose no tokens, and gain what the firing deposits there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each reset place *shall* end holding exactly what the firing deposited there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires and the firing ends with its action, on an executor with output validation enabled ([CONC-026], the default), the places in which it deposits *shall* be exactly the places of one output branch of its output spec, each receiving one or more tokens.<br><br>*When* the transition fires and the firing ends with the timeout outcome, it *shall* deposit in every place as many tokens as the timeout outcome puts there ([IO-013], [IO-014]).<br><br>Deposits are compared per place: the order in which a firing deposits its tokens is not normative, and two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place are the same deposit. | 1. For every transition t:<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which an input place p holds fewer tokens than the required count c of its input arc;<br>3. t does not fire from a marking in which a read place p is unmarked;<br>4. t does not fire from a marking in which an inhibitor place p is marked;<br>5. from every marking at which t is enabled, some firing of t exists (to some marking);<br>6. every firing of t that deposits d leaves an input place p that is not a reset place with what it held, minus the consumption count of its arc, plus what d puts in p;<br>7. every firing of t that deposits d leaves a place p that is neither an input place nor a reset place of t with what it held plus what d puts in p;<br>8. every firing of t that deposits d leaves a reset place p with exactly what d puts in p;<br>9. every firing of t from m that deposits d either puts one or more tokens in each place of some output branch b of t and none in any other place, or puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout outcome d₀ of t for what the firing consumed from m. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>    (∀ (p : N) (c : Card),<br>        InputArc t p c → while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p &lt; requiredCount c, never Fire F t) ∧<br>      (∀ (p : N), ReadArc t p → while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (∀ (p : N), InhibitorArc t p → while fun m ↦ Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>          (∀ (m : CountMarking N), Enabled t m → ∃ m', Fire F t m m') ∧<br>            (∀ (d : List N) (p : N) (c : Card),<br>                InputArc t p c →<br>                  ¬ResetArc t p →<br>                    on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>                      TokenCount m' p =<br>                        TokenCount m p - consumptionCount c (TokenCount m p) +<br>                          Deposits d p) ∧<br>              (∀ (d : List N) (p : N),<br>                  (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) →<br>                    ¬ResetArc t p →<br>                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>                        TokenCount m' p = TokenCount m p + Deposits d p) ∧<br>                (∀ (d : List N) (p : N),<br>                    ResetArc t p →<br>                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦<br>                        TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧<br>                  ∀ (d : List N),<br>                    on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m x ↦<br>                      (∃ b, OutputBranch t b ∧ OnPlacesOf d b) ∨<br>                        ∃ d₀, TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) d₀ ∧ SamePerPlace d d₀</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part, so 'produced on complete' (Output) and 'consumed / removed on fire' (Input, Reset) both land in the one step. 'Able to fire' is read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking.
- Requires token? column. 'Yes' for an input arc is read as 'holds at least the required count' (glossary: Enabled, Required count), which is one token for One and All; 'Yes' for a read arc as 'marked'; 'No (blocks if present)' for an inhibitor arc as 'marked blocks'. The 'No' entries (output, reset, and the inhibitor arc while its place is unmarked) are read together as the fourth line: the table lists every token requirement, so a transition whose input, read and inhibitor arcs are all satisfied can fire whatever its output and reset places hold.
- Consumes? column. 'Yes' for an input arc is read as the consumption count of IO-007 (glossary: Consumption count). 'No' for output, inhibitor and read arcs is the sixth line: a place that only those arcs touch loses nothing. 'Yes (all)' for a reset arc is the seventh line (glossary: Deposit): a reset place that is also an output place keeps what the firing deposited there, and a reset place that is also an input place ends with the deposit too, so the fifth line excludes reset places.
- The fifth line uses truncated subtraction, as Seam.fireNC does; under the first line the subtraction never truncates, because a firing only starts when every input place holds at least its required count.
- Effect column, Output ('Token produced on complete') is the outcome line, the last line of the reading, which reads the eighth, ninth and tenth sentences quoted together. A firing relation does not record how a firing ended. As IO-012 says, a firing ends with its action when it does not end with the timeout outcome, and a firing whose deposit puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout-outcome deposit of the transition from the same marking may have ended with the timeout outcome. So the eighth and ninth sentences are read as one disjunction: the deposit marks exactly the places of an output branch (eighth: the branch fixes which places receive tokens, one or more each, not how many; glossary: Output branch, Produced set), or it equals a timeout outcome per place (ninth: as many tokens in every place). A transition with no output spec has the one empty branch, so it deposits nothing. Read ('Token remains') is the sixth line. Inhibitor ('Disables transition') is the third line.
- Tenth sentence (deposits are compared per place). Every line of the reading reads the deposit d only through Deposits d (the produced set of d is the set of places p with Deposits d p ≠ 0), so two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place satisfy it alike and the order of d plays no part: core036_c8_perPlace shows it for the outcome line, and core036_perPlace_closed shows that closing any firing relation under per-place equal deposits keeps CORE-036. Lines 5 to 7 already compare per place.
- The outcome line is scoped by CONC-026: F is read as the firing relation of an executor with output validation enabled, the default. With the CONC-026 skip enabled a firing that ends with its action deposits what the action wrote, as CONC-026 says, and the outcome line is not claimed of it; lines 1 to 7 hold of every executor.
- TimeoutOutcome reads the first Timeout node in pre-order. A transition that builds holds at most one Timeout node and no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child (IO-013, IO-014), so that node's outcome is the timeout outcome. Transitions that building rejects (IO-011 to IO-014) are not transitions of any net (CORE-022); the statement still ranges over every Trans, and the reference semantics satisfies it for all of them, so it needs no well-formedness premise. That at most one output branch matches a deposit (IO-012) is not part of CORE-036: the outcome line asks for some branch.
- Read, 'provides value': the value of the read token is not visible at token-count granularity; that the action receives it is CORE-032 AC3, not encoded here.
- Input token order (FIFO, CORE-030 AC2) and output token timestamps (CORE-035 AC2, IO-014 AC5) are below token-count granularity and not encoded here.
- AC1 (each arc type behaves exactly as described in the table) is the whole statement: one line per cell of the 'Requires token?' column (lines 1 to 4) and of the 'Consumes?' and 'Effect' columns (lines 5 to 7 and the outcome line), as laid out in the assumptions above.
- AC2 (an action that writes two tokens into one place of the branch it satisfies fires, and the marking receives all of them) is CORE_036_allows_multi: CORE-036 holds of a firing relation in which t: a → and(b, c) fires with the write b, b, c, and that firing leaves 2 tokens in b and 1 in c. That such a write is deposited at all is IO-015 and IO-016 AC4; CORE-036 only has to allow it.
- AC3 (two firings that deposit the same number of tokens in every place, in different orders, deposit the same outcome) is core036_c8_perPlace and core036_perPlace_closed, and concretely CORE_036_allows_multi: the write c, b, b of the same transition is allowed alike and leaves the same marking.
- InputArc names the first input arc on a place (glossary: Input arc); CORE-030 rejects a transition with two input arcs on one place at build, so for every well-formed transition it is the only one.
