<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_014"></a>
## IO-014: Output ForwardInput

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_014` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `992343cae7b2121d`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| `ForwardInput(from, to)` is a node of an output spec that, on the timeout outcome, deposits in `to` the tokens a firing consumed from its input place `from`.<br><br>*If* a `ForwardInput` node of an output spec is not inside the child of a `Timeout` node, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with<br><br>naming the first such node in the order the spec is written (pre-order, children left to right).<br><br>The check runs when the transition is built, on every construction path, as the check of [IO-011] does.<br><br>*When* a firing ends with the timeout outcome, every `ForwardInput(from, to)` in the `Timeout` child *shall* deposit in `to` one token for each token the firing consumed from `from`, carrying the token's value, in consumption order.<br><br>The count *shall* be the consumption count of the input arc on `from` ([IO-007]): 1 for `One`, `n` for `Exactly(n)`, and the whole drained batch for `All` and `AtLeast(m)`.<br><br>*If* a firing consumed more than one token from `from`, *then* the forward *shall not* deposit fewer tokens in `to` than the firing consumed; in particular it *shall not* forward only the first consumed token.<br><br>*If* a firing consumed no token from `from`, which a declared input cannot do but a mis-declared spec can, *then* the forward *shall* deposit no token in `to`. | 1. Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg) and T the firings that end with the timeout outcome.<br>2. For every transition t whose output spec o has a ForwardInput(from, to) outside the child of a Timeout node, the first in pre-order, building t fails;<br>3. and if t's input places are distinct, no output branch of o names a place twice, o has at most one Timeout node and no Xor node inside its Timeout child, building t fails with the IO-014 message naming t, from and to.<br>4. For every transition t whose output spec has a ForwardInput from a place that is not one of t's input places, building t fails.<br>5. Every transition that passes every build check (distinct input places, no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every forward from an input place, no two output branches claiming one set of places) builds.<br>6. For every transition t whose output spec has at most one Timeout node and a ForwardInput(from, to) anywhere in that node's child (also under And or Xor), every deposit d and every firing of t from m in T that deposits d, there is one timeout deposit e of the Timeout child, built with every ForwardInput(a, b) of the child putting in b one token per token the firing consumes from a, such that e puts no more tokens than d in any place (no consumed token is lost, at any forward of the child) and d puts no more tokens than e in any place (one token per consumed token, none extra). | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build T ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src dst : N),<br>      OutputSpec t = some o → forwardOutside o = some (src, dst) → Build t ≠ none) ∧<br>    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src dst : N),<br>        OutputSpec t = some o →<br>          forwardOutside o = some (src, dst) →<br>            PreOutputChecks t →<br>              ¬DupBranch o →<br>                timeoutCount o ≤ 1 →<br>                  xorInTimeout o = false → Build t = some (msgForward t src dst)) ∧<br>      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src : N),<br>          OutputSpec t = some o →<br>            src ∈ forwardSources o → src ∉ inPlaces t → Build t ≠ none) ∧<br>        (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), Builds t → Build t = none) ∧<br>          ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (src dst : N),<br>            (∀ (o : Out N), OutputSpec t = some o → timeoutCount o ≤ 1) →<br>              TimeoutForwards t src dst →<br>                ∀ (d : List N),<br>                  on fun m m' ↦ T t m d m', shall fun m x ↦<br>                    ∃ e,<br>                      TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) e ∧<br>                        (∀ (p : N), Deposits e p ≤ Deposits d p) ∧<br>                          ∀ (p : N), Deposits d p ≤ Deposits e p</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (Build, T). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the reference builder refBuild runs the CORE-030 input-arc check and then the output-spec checks in the order of the output composition preamble of spec/02-input-output-specs.md (IO-011, IO-013's Timeout count, IO-013's Xor inside the Timeout child, IO-014, IO-014 AC3, IO-012), with each message byte for byte except CORE-030's, which the spec does not give. Place names are rendered with the place type's ToString.
- T is the relation of firings that end with the timeout outcome (glossary: Timeout outcome), read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the Timeout child's tokens (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A plain FireRel cannot be used: on Timeout(ForwardInput(from, to)) the action branch [to] and a forward of one token are the same deposit. The witness refTimedOutFire is the part of RefFire whose outcome is a timedOut choice (refTimedOutFire_refFire). That the resulting marking receives d is the effect rule (CORE-030, CORE-034, CORE-035) on the plain firing relation, not restated here.
- The build error is msgForward, byte for byte: output spec of transition '<t>' uses ForwardInput('<from>', '<to>') outside the child of a Timeout node; a forward deposits only on the timeout outcome (IO-014). 'Not inside the child of a Timeout node' and 'the first such node' are forwardOutside: the pre-order walk, children left to right, that does not enter a Timeout node. The preamble's order runs the IO-011 check (a place twice in one output branch) and the IO-013 checks (more than one Timeout node, an Xor node inside the Timeout child) first, so on such a spec the message is theirs, and the second line only requires that building fails; CORE-030's input-arc check is not placed by the preamble and is treated the same way.
- 'On every construction path' is read as: Build is the one builder every construction path goes through (builders, composition, channel merge, fusion), so a transition that a path yields builds exactly when Build accepts it. Which paths exist is not in the model. No executor option reaches Build (CONC-026).
- The fifth line is the converse that makes 'builds' checkable (AC7's specs that build): a transition passing the checks before the output spec (CORE-030, the IO-002/IO-004 input counts and EXEC-012's input-and-read check, PreOutputChecks) and every build check of the output composition preamble builds. The checks are the glossary terms Builds and WellFormedOut, the same checks IO-013 reads.
- The firing line is stated for every transition whose output spec has at most one Timeout node, not only for transitions that build: a transition with two or more Timeout nodes is rejected (IO-013) and has no single Timeout child, so no reading of 'the Timeout child' is claimed there, while a transition with a forward from a non-input place, rejected by the fourth line, is still covered, which is what keeps the fourth quote (no input consumed, nothing forwarded) checkable. A transition with one Timeout node has one Timeout child, the one Out.findTimeout finds.
- 'The `ForwardInput(from, to)` node of an output spec that, on the timeout outcome, deposits in `to` the tokens a firing consumed' (first quote) is the firing line, which says how many.
- 'Every ForwardInput(from, to) in the Timeout child' includes a ForwardInput nested under And or Xor. On a transition that builds the child holds no Xor node (IO-013), so it has one timeout deposit (glossary: timeoutOutcome_unique); the line is also stated for transitions that do not build, where an Xor child has several timeout deposits and which one a firing chose is visible only in the whole deposit, so the statement compares d place by place with one timeout deposit e of the child (glossary: Timeout outcome, TimeoutOutcome); deposits are compared per place, so the order of the deposit list does not matter (CORE-036). This also fixes the tokens the child's Place leaves put in, which is IO-013's subject (AC5); it is restated here only because it is what identifies the chosen alternative. Comparing only the place `to` would let a forward-first firing pass whenever another alternative of the child happens to put the same count in `to`.
- 'The count' (sixth quote) is the firing's consumption from `from`, the glossary term Consume (Consumes t m from), which is IO-007's consumption count of the input arc on `from` (bridge lemma consumes_eq) and 0 for a place with no input arc. The two bounds of the firing line together say d equals e place by place, with one existential e for both; they are split so that losing tokens and inventing tokens are refuted separately.
- The seventh quote (no forward of fewer tokens, not only the first) is the first bound. The eighth quote (no input consumed, nothing forwarded) is the second bound, e having no forwarded token where Consumes t m from = 0.
- The sentence '*When* a `ForwardInput` forwards a consumed token, the token it deposits in `to` *shall* carry the consumed token's `created_at` as well as its value.' is token metadata (a value and a creation stamp) below the count granularity of the firing semantics, which has no token values or stamps; it is not encoded, and neither is the paragraph around it (the TIME-015 exception, the NU-022 tie-break).
- AC1 (from must be a declared input place, validated at build time) and AC3 (an invalid from reference is a build error) are the fourth line. Which forward AC3's existing message names when several are invalid is not said by the text; the reference builder names the first in pre-order, and the statement does not constrain the message.
- AC2 (one token per consumed token, preserving values and consumption order) is the firing line for its count; values and consumption order are below the count granularity and are not encoded.
- AC4 (All or Exactly(n) with N tokens consumed puts exactly N in `to`) is the two bounds together, with Consumes giving N for Exactly(n) and the whole place for All.
- AC5 (a forwarded token's created_at equals the original's and is not re-stamped from the epoch clock, while a minted recovery token is, in every implementation) is token metadata below the count granularity and is not encoded.
- AC6 (every analysis deposits what the executor deposits) is about the verifier's branch expansion (IO-016, VER-001), not about firings or building; Novel/ForwardDeposit.lean proves it for the flattened rows.
- AC7 is the second, third and fifth lines: its three rejected specs (ForwardInput(a, b), Xor(c, ForwardInput(a, b)), And(c, Xor(e, ForwardInput(a, b)))) fail with the message naming a and b, and its two accepted specs (Timeout(d, ForwardInput(a, b)), Xor(c, Timeout(d, And(e, ForwardInput(a, b))))) build, under the reference builder with a an input place (IO_014_ac7_rejected, IO_014_ac7_builds).
- Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_015"></a>
## IO-015: Output Validation

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_015` · Kind **F** · Scope every declared output spec · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `61ac6b8b57fcb0a7`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| An *assignment* selects exactly one child at each `Xor` node it reaches; nodes beneath an unselected `Xor` child are never evaluated.<br><br>*If* exactly one assignment claims a set *equal* to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* succeed.<br><br>*If* no assignment claims a set equal to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* fail, because nothing explains what was written.<br><br>*If* two or more assignments claim a set equal to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* fail, because the write is genuinely ambiguous.<br><br>For a transition that builds, no two assignments claim the same set ([IO-012]), so on a firing this third case does not arise.<br><br>The comparison is over **sets of places**: a spec names places, not counts, so an action that deposits several tokens into one claimed place conforms. | 1. For every declared output spec o and every deposit d, with assignment i of o claiming the i-th entry of Out.branches o:<br>2. if some assignment i claims exactly the produced set of d and every assignment that does is i, validation of d against o succeeds;<br>3. if no assignment claims exactly the produced set of d, validation fails;<br>4. if two different assignments i ≠ j both claim exactly the produced set of d, validation fails. | <pre>fun {N} V ↦<br>  (∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N) (i : ℕ),<br>      ExactAssignment o d i → (∀ (j : ℕ), ExactAssignment o d j → j = i) → V o d = true) ∧<br>    (∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N), (∀ (i : ℕ), ¬ExactAssignment o d i) → V o d = false) ∧<br>      ∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N) (i j : ℕ),<br>        i ≠ j → ExactAssignment o d i → ExactAssignment o d j → V o d = false</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A validator is the verdict function of one implementation: its inputs are the declared output spec and the tokens the completed action produced, as a deposit (a list of places with repetition); its output is success (true) or violation (false). The produced set is the places of the deposit (glossary: Produced set).
- When an action completes, an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]), shall validate its produced set against the transition's output spec. This sentence is the trigger and is not encoded: the block fixes the verdict of the check, not when it runs. An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled runs no check, so the verdict constrains nothing there (CONC-026's subject). A completion that fails validation deposits no outcome and is not a firing (glossary: Fire); a transition with no output spec has nothing to validate; the timeout outcome (IO-013) does not complete the action and is not validated.
- Assignments are counted, not their claims: two assignments that claim the same set are two (Xor(A, A) with A produced has two exact assignments and fails). Out.branches enumerates one claim per assignment, in the claim rules of the bullet list; n-ary And and Xor are read as right-nested binary nodes, which changes neither the number of assignments, their claims nor their IO-016 order.
- The verdict function is total: the three clauses range over every output spec, those IO-012 rejects at build included. The sentence 'For a transition that builds, no two assignments claim the same set' is a consequence, not a clause: the glossary's WellFormedOut is the build-time constraint on an output spec, and on a spec satisfying it no two different assignments are exact for any deposit (theorem IO_015_wf_noAmbiguous), so under IO-015 the verdict is success exactly when some assignment is exact (theorem IO_015_wf_iff). The theorems use only its IO-012 conjunct, pairwise distinct branch sets.
- The set-of-places sentence is a consequence, not a clause: the three clauses fix the verdict from the number of exact assignments (theorem IO_015_determines), and that number reads only the produced set (theorem IO_015_setOnly). Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): two deposits with the same count in every place, in any order, get the same verdict (theorem IO_015_perPlace).
- AC1 (conforming output → success) is the first clause, 'conforming' read as 'exactly one exact assignment'.
- AC2 (non-conforming output → failure event emitted) and AC3 (consumed input tokens are not restored on failure) are executor behaviour on a failed completion ('Validation failure is treated as a transition failure', EVT-007); the failure is not a firing of the reference semantics, which has no failed completion, so neither is encoded here.
- AC4 (zero exact assignments → violation; two or more → violation) is the second and third clauses.
- AC5 (Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B)) with A, B, C produced → success) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac5).
- AC6 (output spec declared, action produces nothing → validation failure on every firing) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 and every output spec (theorem IO_015_ac6): every claim names at least one place, so none equals the empty produced set. That the built-in passthrough is rejected before execution is CORE-043's subject.
- AC7 (mid-action publication) fixes which tokens make up the deposit the validator sees (published places count) and that published tokens stay in the marking on a violation; both are executor behaviour outside the verdict function and are not encoded. With the published places in the deposit, the AC7 verdicts (And(A, B) with A, B produced → success; with A only → violation) are checked on the reference validator.
- AC8 (And is unordered) is not a separate clause: a claim is compared as a set, and permuting the children of an And permutes the assignments and the order of places within a claim. It is checked for the AC8 pair And(A, Xor(D, E)) / And(Xor(D, E), A) on every produced set drawn from A, D, E and one foreign place, the empty one included (theorem IO_015_ac8).
- AC9 (Xor(And(A, C), B) with B and C produced → violation) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac9).
- AC10 (Xor(And(A, Xor(D, E)), A) with only A produced → success) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac10).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_015_firing"></a>
## IO-015: Output validation: a validated write is deposited

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_015_firing` · Kind **B** · Scope executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026) · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `af6e82b5561b0880`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* exactly one assignment claims a set *equal* to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* succeed.<br><br>The comparison is over **sets of places**: a spec names places, not counts, so an action that deposits several tokens into one claimed place conforms. | 1. For every transition t with output spec o, every marking m at which t is enabled and every deposit d such that exactly one assignment of o claims exactly the produced set of d:<br>2. some firing of t from m deposits d. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),<br>    OutputSpec t = some o →<br>      ∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>        Enabled t m →<br>          ∀ (d : List N),<br>            (∃ i, ExactAssignment o d i ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ), ExactAssignment o d j → j = i) →<br>              ∃ m', F t m d m'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The firing-level reading of the IO-015 sentences quoted: the block IO_015 fixes the validator's verdict; this one ties the verdict to firings. An action may write any tokens (glossary: Deposit), a completion that passes validation deposits what the action wrote, and one that fails is not a firing (glossary: Fire). So every write that validation accepts is the deposit of some firing. 'Conforms' is read as 'passes validation and is deposited', as IO-016 AC4 says of such a write ('the tokens are deposited regardless').
- Timing and priority play no part: whether the action completes within a Timeout budget is nondeterministic (IO-013), so a validated write is always one way a firing can end.
- CORE-036 compares deposits per place and asks only that the places a firing deposits in be the places of one output branch, each receiving one or more tokens, so it allows such a deposit: both blocks hold of the validated-write executor (theorem CORE_036_IO_015_firing_consistent).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_015_firing_validated` (Libpetri.Spec.Clashes): ✓ `IO_015_firing` holds of the validated-write firings (`refFireValidated`): a write with exactly one exact assignment passes the reference validator (`IO_015_reference`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], IO_015_firing refFireValidated</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_015_firing_forbids_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Clashes): ✗ The reference semantics deposits exactly one token per claimed place, so the leaf `Place(0)` never deposits the validated write `[0, 0]`.
  <pre>¬IO_015_firing RefFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_015_firing_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Clashes): `IO_015_firing` is exercised: the reference validator accepts `[0, 0]` for `Place(0)`, the validated-write firings fire it from the empty marking, and it is not an output branch.
  <pre>ioRefValidate (Out.place 0) [0, 0] = true ∧<br>  (∃ m', refFireValidated (clashT (Out.place 0)) clashEmpty [0, 0] m') ∧<br>    ¬OutputBranch (clashT (Out.place 0)) [0, 0]</pre>
- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_036_IO_015_firing_consistent` (Libpetri.Spec.Clashes): ✓ CORE-036 and `IO_015_firing` hold together: the validated-write firings satisfy both. They are the reference firings with more deposits, and every extra deposit marks exactly the places of one output branch, which is what CORE-036's outcome line asks of a firing that ends with its action.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N],<br>  CORE_036 refFireValidated ∧ IO_015_firing refFireValidated</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_016"></a>
## IO-016: Branch Enumeration

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_016` · Kind **F** · Scope all output specs · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `88c2b9b595b1495c`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The branch enumeration of a `Place` node *shall* be one output branch, holding that place.<br><br>The branch enumeration of a `ForwardInput(from, to)` node *shall* be one output branch, holding `to`.<br><br>The branch enumeration of an `And` node *shall* be the Cartesian product of its children's branch enumerations: one output branch for each choice of one output branch per child, holding the union of the chosen output branches, with the first child's choice varying slowest.<br><br>The branch enumeration of an `Xor` node *shall* be the union of its children's branch enumerations: one output branch for each output branch of each child, the first child's output branches first.<br><br>The branch enumeration of a `Timeout` node *shall* be its child's branch enumeration. | 1. Place(p) enumerates exactly the one branch {p};<br>2. ForwardInput(from, to) enumerates exactly the one branch {to};<br>3. And(l, r) enumerates, for each branch x of l in order and, within it, each branch y of r in order, the branch x ∪ y, and nothing else;<br>4. Xor(l, r) enumerates the branches of l, in order, then the branches of r, in order, each as often as it occurs there, and nothing else;<br>5. Timeout(c) enumerates exactly the branches of c, in order. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] E ↦<br>  (∀ (p : N), E (Out.place p) = [{p}]) ∧<br>    (∀ (s d : N), E (Out.forward s d) = [{d}]) ∧<br>      (∀ (l r : Out N), E (l.and r) = branchCross (E l) (E r)) ∧<br>        (∀ (l r : Out N), E (l.xor r) = E l ++ E r) ∧ ∀ (c : Out N), E c.timeout = E c</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A branch enumeration is a function from an output spec alone to a list of output branches, so it is static by its type. A branch is a set of places (`Finset`), as the text says ("a set of places: it says which places receive a token when the branch is taken, not how many"). The list keeps multiplicity (`Xor(P, P)` has two branches) and its order: the lines compare lists with equality, so the enumeration is fixed exactly (`IO_016_unique`). The order is normative because the analyses expand a transition into its branches "in the order above" and name the virtual transitions `<t>_b<i>` in enumeration order ([VER-001]), which the byte-identical SMT scripts carry ([VER-013]).
- An n-ary `And` or `Xor` is read as right-nested binary nodes, as `Reference.Out` writes it. List append and the lexicographic Cartesian product are associative and union is associative, so the nesting changes neither the branches nor their order: the n-ary product with the first child slowest is the right-nested product of binary ones.
- A branch read as a set loses a repeated claim: `And(P, P)` enumerates {P}, while the reference `Out.branches` lists [P, P]. IO-011 rejects such a spec when it is built, so on every buildable spec the two agree (`IO_016_card_of_wf`: each set has as many places as the list it reads).
- The list has one entry per assignment (IO-015), counted by position, so on a spec that builds no two entries are the same set: IO-012 rejects at build time any spec with two distinct assignments claiming one set, and its check enumerates per IO-016 and compares the entries as sets in index order (the numbering of VER-001's `<t>_b<i>`). The paragraph saying so is a consequence of IO-012's build check, not a further constraint on the enumeration; it is derived, not stated (`IO_016_nodup_of_wf`). The enumeration itself is defined on every spec, ambiguous ones included, because the build check is computed from it.
- A spec that builds holds at most one `Timeout` node, and a `ForwardInput` only inside that node's child (IO-013, IO-014). The `Timeout` and `ForwardInput` lines still fix the enumeration on every spec: the enumeration is a total function on output specs, and the build checks read it before a spec is known to build.
- AC1 (`And(P1, P2)` → {P1, P2}) follows from lines 1 and 3; AC2 (`Xor(P1, P2)` → {P1}, {P2}) from lines 1 and 4; AC3 (`Xor(And(P1, P2), P3)` → {P1, P2}, {P3}) from lines 1, 3 and 4. The non-vacuity theorem checks all three on the reference enumeration.
- AC4 (the executor's WARN log-message event when a validated firing deposits more than one token in a place its matched branch names, at most once per transition per execution) is an [EVT-013] event of a running executor, and is skipped with the rest of validation by the CONC-026 option. Neither the branch enumeration nor the firing relation has an event store or an execution; it is not encoded here and needs a behaviour block over executions.
- A branch fixes which places receive tokens, not how many: with output validation enabled, a firing that ends with its action deposits one or more tokens in each place of one output branch and none in any other (glossary: Output branch, IO-015, CORE-036). The paragraph on what the analyses deposit (one token per place of a branch: VER-010, VER-001, NU-051) describes those analyses, not the enumeration, and is their subject. The reference firing semantics deposits one token per claim of a branch, the case the analyses model; the non-vacuity theorem shows one such firing.
- The paragraph on the timeout outcome says that it is not an output branch (glossary: Timeout outcome), which the `Timeout` line respects by enumerating the child's branches only; the `ForwardInput` line is the branch an action writes, `to` claimed once (glossary: Forward, IO-015), not the timeout outcome's per-consumed-token deposit (IO-014). How the analyses append the timeout outcome after the branches, when it differs place by place from every branch (deposits compared per place, CORE-036), is VER-001's subject.
- The block fixes the enumeration function only. That executors and analyses use it (the executor's validation, the SCG virtual transitions, the flattener) is the subject of IO-015, VER-001 and VER-010.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_016_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_016): The reference enumeration satisfies IO-016: `Out.branches` is `[[p]]` on a place, `[[to]]` on a forward, `cross` (concatenation of one branch per child, left child slowest) on `And`, append on `Xor` and the child's on `Timeout`; read as sets, concatenation is union (`map_toFinset_cross`). Each line holds with equality, in the reference order.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], IO_016 refBranchSets</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_016_forbids_andAsXor` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_016): ✗ Reading `And` like `Xor` violates IO-016 (third line): `And(0, 1)` enumerates the two branches {0}, {1} instead of the one branch {0, 1}.
  <pre>¬IO_016 io016_andAsXor</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_016_forbids_forwardNone` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_016): ✗ Dropping a forward from the enumeration violates IO-016 (second line): `ForwardInput(0, 1)` enumerates no branch instead of {1}.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_017"></a>
## IO-017: allPlaces Flattening

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_017` · Kind **F** · Scope all output specs · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `bc11b32a87ffc708`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The `allPlaces` set of a `Place` node *shall* be the set holding only that place.<br><br>The `allPlaces` set of a `ForwardInput(from, to)` node *shall* be the set holding only `to`.<br><br>The `allPlaces` set of an `And` node *shall* be the union of its children's `allPlaces` sets.<br><br>The `allPlaces` set of an `Xor` node *shall* be the union of its children's `allPlaces` sets.<br><br>The `allPlaces` set of a `Timeout` node *shall* be its child's `allPlaces` set. | 1. Place(p) gives exactly the set {p};<br>2. ForwardInput(from, to) gives exactly the set {to};<br>3. And(l, r) gives exactly the union of the sets of l and r;<br>4. Xor(l, r) gives exactly the union of the sets of l and r;<br>5. Timeout(c) gives exactly the set of c. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] A ↦<br>  (∀ (p : N), A (Out.place p) = {p}) ∧<br>    (∀ (s d : N), A (Out.forward s d) = {d}) ∧<br>      (∀ (l r : Out N), A (l.and r) = A l ∪ A r) ∧<br>        (∀ (l r : Out N), A (l.xor r) = A l ∪ A r) ∧ ∀ (c : Out N), A c.timeout = A c</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A place-set function is a function from an output spec alone to a finite set of places (`Finset`), so it is static by its type and has no order and no repetition: the text and every runtime return a set (Rust `HashSet<PlaceRef>`, Java `Set<Place<?>>`, TypeScript `Set<Place<any>>`). The lines compare sets with equality, so they fix the function exactly (`IO_017_unique`).
- The lines say "be" and "holding only": the set equals the places the text names, so it is complete (every place, every `Xor` alternative, every `Timeout` child) and exact (nothing else). The markdown's prose ("collect all leaf places") and test derivation ("complete set") state completeness only; the block reads collecting the leaf places as returning them and nothing else, which is what all three runtimes do (Rust `rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs` `collect_places`, Java `Arc.java` `allPlaces`, TypeScript `out.ts` `collectPlaces`). The containment reading is strictly weaker (`IO_017_mutant_superset_killed`), and a `Place` leaf that also names another place is forbidden (`IO_017_forbids_placeExtra`).
- The statement is generic in the place type `N` and its equality, so it fixes no place identity: it holds for whatever identity a runtime compares places by. Rust's set compares `PlaceRef` by name and Java's set compares `Place` records by name and token type (MOD-024). TypeScript's `Set` holds place objects by reference, so two distinct place objects with one name are two members there; on a net whose places have distinct names the three agree. The model writes places as names (CORE-002), and the glossary entry Same set of places, like the EARS lines, leaves place equality to the implementation (CORE-002, MOD-024).
- An n-ary `And` or `Xor` is read as right-nested binary nodes, as `Reference.Out` writes it and IO-016 does. Union is associative, so the nesting does not change the set. An `And` with one child (the runtimes allow it; an `Xor` needs two) is that child, which the n-ary union also gives.
- The second line strengthens AC2 (`ForwardInput(from, to)` contributes `to`), which does not say that `from` is left out: it reads AC2 as contributing `to` and nothing else. It says "only `to`" rather than "not `from`" because `from` and `to` may be one place, and then the set holds it. The reading follows the text: the prose collects the places the spec writes to, `from` is an input place (IO-014), and all three runtimes add only `to` (Rust `rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs` `collect_places`, Java `Arc.java` `allPlaces`, TypeScript `out.ts` `collectPlaces`). The glossary entries Forward ("In an output branch it claims `to`") and Output arc (a place the output spec names) say the same, so a forward makes `to`, not `from`, an output arc.
- The function is defined on every output spec, ones that fail a build-time check included: the `Timeout` and `ForwardInput` lines fix it whether or not the spec has one `Timeout` node and its forwards inside that node's child (IO-013, IO-014), since the build checks and the glossary read it before a spec is known to build.
- AC1 (`Xor(And(P1, P2), Timeout(5s, P3))` gives {P1, P2, P3}) follows from lines 1, 3, 4 and 5; the timeout's duration does not matter, since `Reference.Out` carries none and the fifth line reads only the child. AC2 is the second line. The non-vacuity theorem checks both on the reference function, and the test derivation (a nested spec gives the complete set) is AC1.
- The relation to IO-016 is derived, not stated: the set is the union of the output branches of the branch enumeration (`IO_017_union_of_branches`, for every pair of functions that satisfy IO-016 and IO-017). So is the relation to the glossary's output arcs (`IO_017_outputArc`).
- The block fixes the function only. That the output specification offers it as a method is an API fact of each runtime and is not encoded. That executors and analyses read output places through it (CORE-035, CORE-062, CORE-072, VER-001) is the subject of those requirements.

## NU-051: EXTENDED Coloured-Consumer Fragment

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_051` · Kind **F** · Scope the fragment classifier of every ν verifier · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `393227da1832a575`

**Assumptions**

- The classifier is per transition, as the glossary term Fragment classifier reads it: no role for one transition means the net falls back to the sound over-approximation ([NU-050]); the Rust `classify` (rust/libpetri-verification/src/name_fragment.rs) returns no fragment for the net as soon as one transition is refused. The coloured set is an argument. How a verifier builds it (the match keys, and under EXTENDED the declared carriers and the relay targets of [NU-054]) is the verifier pipeline's subject (W10), not a line here. So every line speaks of the places coloured in the mode at hand: a place coloured only by a declared carrier or a relay target is not coloured under BASE, where the coloured set is the match keys alone.
- The first paragraph of the section is not a line. Its sentence 'Both are decided solely by the solver-free Route B quotient' conflicts with [NU-053], which lets Route A decide the EXTENDED fragment, and with AC7 and AC8, which speak of both routes (clash nu-c#1, ruling D20 open). The two-value knob, BASE as the default and its builder option names are configuration (kind N); the key format is [VER-012]'s subject.
- Line 1 is the first quoted sentence. It is the BASE half of AC1 for a fixture whose consumed place is coloured under BASE, that is a match key of the net (the coloured place a mint feeds): a consumer of a place coloured only by an EXTENDED carrier or relay target consumes no coloured place under BASE, gets an ordinary role there, and the net is not refused on its account. Whether a given fixture's place is coloured in each mode is the coloured-set computation (W10). Line 2 is the second quoted sentence (the prose: 'The analyzer' takes such a transition 'only as a drain/relay role and only when it consumes exactly one coloured input at count exactly one'; 'A consumer that consumes more than one coloured place, or consumes at any count other than one (`Exactly(n≥2)`, `AtLeast`, `All`), is rejected') and AC2, and its last conjunct is the third quoted sentence and the Route B half of AC8: a timeout write into a coloured place that is a unit token or a forward of another input leaves the transition with no role. Its first conjunct (SingleColouredWrites: every branch puts exactly one token into each coloured place it writes, and no drained batch, a forward from an `All` or `AtLeast` input whose count is read off the marking ([IO-014]), into one) is the clause 'puts on each branch exactly one token, and never a drained batch' of the second quoted sentence. The markdown gives it only as the reason for refusing higher input counts ('the base marking adds exactly one token per output place, so re-emitting a higher input cardinality into the name layer would over-count'); the shipped classifier refuses on it (`classifyT`, the branch check), and so does the line.
- Line 3 is the fourth quoted sentence and the EXTENDED half of AC1: the role is given, not only allowed (the markdown's 'MAY consume' is a permission to the net author; the classifier that the author relies on then has to give the role). Its premises are the sentence's conditions one for one: one coloured input at count one, no test arc on a coloured place (line 4), one token and no drained batch per coloured place a branch writes (SingleColouredWrites, as in line 2), and only forwards of that input on timeout (ForwardsOnly, as in line 2). A transition that builds has SingleColouredWrites whenever its coloured timeout writes forward its one coloured input: an output branch names a place at most once ([IO-011]), and that input is consumed at count one, so its forward deposits one token. The model takes the branches and the timeout writes as two separate arguments, so the line states the premise.
- The mint declaration plays no part in lines 1 to 3 and 6, which hold for both values of declared; the role sentence says so ('whether or not it is declared a mint'). This agrees with [NU-010], whose mint writes a coloured place without consuming one: a declared transition that consumes a coloured place is a consumer here, and the mint rule (Novel.RouteB.classifyS_mint) is [NU-010]'s verifier line, not this block's.
- 'Because the consumed count is fixed at one, the role is identified by the input place name alone' is encoded by lines 2 and 3, which fix the role to `consume s.place`: Role.consume carries a place and nothing else.
- Line 4 is the fifth quoted sentence and AC3. The prose says the analyzer rejects a net in which 'any coloured place carries' such an arc 'on any transition'; per transition that is line 4, and the net falls back because one of its transitions gets no role. Its reason ('it never turns a `Proven`/`Violated` into an unsound verdict') is [NU-050]'s soundness, not a line.
- Line 5 is the sixth quoted sentence and the first half of AC7. 'A non-coloured non-key input (a budget or permit) is unaffected' is not a line: line 5 speaks only of coloured inputs, and NU_051_nonvacuous shows a join with an uncoloured budget input that gets its join role. The second half of AC7 ('a stranding such a net can reach is not reported `Proven`') is a verdict and waits for the verifier pipeline (W10).
- Line 6 is the seventh quoted sentence, the converse of lines 1 to 3: the coloured-consumer role exists only under EXTENDED ('BASE reproduces the shipped mint → matched-join fragment exactly'), only for 'a transition with **no** match spec' (a matched transition takes a name by its match test, [NU-020], not by the consumer step), and only for a transition that consumes a coloured place (the relay step removes the name 'from its coloured input'). With line 2 it pins down every transition the role is given to.
- The relay and drain semantics ('A coloured consumer relays the consumed name-symbol into each coloured output of the fired branch ... or drains it ... on a branch that produces no coloured output') is the block NU_051_relay. AC6 (MAY: one `Xor` consumer relays on one branch and drains on another) is permitted by lines 2 and 3, which do not depend on the branches: the fixture of NU_051_nonvacuous is such a consumer, and NU_051_relay_nonvacuous relays on one branch and drains on the other.
- The relay/drain action precondition is an assumption on the net author (kind A), not a line: the action threads the consumed name into its coloured outputs, or into none, and never mints a fresh name while consuming a coloured token. No analysis can check it. It enters Route B as the consumer contract of the name step (`Novel.RouteB.Contract`, under which `name_step_simulates_exec` holds), the premise of [NU-050]'s soundness (W9). 'MUST be documented as such' is a documentation duty (kind Q). 'the report of a verdict names the consumers whose action writes it assumes' is a report line of the verifier pipeline (W10).
- The carrier bullet is not a line yet. Where a declared carrier that is not a place of the net must fail is ruling D95 (clash nu-c#2: AC4 has no mode, the body ignores carriers under BASE, and Java and TypeScript reject at the builder while Rust refuses only on some Route B paths), so AC4 waits for it and for the verifier pipeline (W10). That the carriers join the coloured set before roles are given, and are ignored under BASE, is the coloured-set computation of the pipeline (W10).
- The diagnosability bullet (an 'EXTENDED declined' note) is a report line (kind N) of the verifier pipeline (W10); whether every refusal must carry it is clash nu-c#10 (ruling D20 open).
- AC5 (SHOULD: an end-to-end quiescence verdict on a carrier fixture, attributable to Route B) is a verdict and report line of the verifier pipeline (W10) and depends on the carrier line (D95).
- AC8's executor half (with the minting forks m1, m2, the consumers r1, r2 and a join on KA and KB, the executor reaches done and `placeBound(done, 0)` is not `Proven`) is a verdict line (W10, with the reference ν firing of W9). Its Route A half is Novel.RouteA.shipped_consume, cited by NU_051_routeA_consume, and is not a line: the timeout sentence speaks of the fragment classifier, which is Route B's, and no Route A classifier is abstracted here, because whether Route A decides the EXTENDED fragment at all is clash nu-c#1 (ruling D20 open). Its last sentence ('A consumer whose timeout forwards its coloured input is still a relay') is line 3 with a forward of the consumed input, shown in NU_051_nonvacuous.
- AC2's 'no false `Proven` from an over-counted name layer, no dropped base-enabled firing' is the soundness the refusal buys ([NU-050], W9); the block states the refusal.
- Whether a transition is a mint (declared, and writing no coloured place on timeout) is [NU-010]'s verifier line (Novel.RouteB.classifyS_mint), not this block's.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_051_relay"></a>
## NU-051: EXTENDED Coloured-Consumer Fragment

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay` · Kind **F** · Scope the name layer of Route B · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `14c65885d2d499bd`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a coloured consumer fires on a branch with a name its coloured input holds, the name layer *shall* remove one token of that name from the input, add one token of that name to each coloured output of the branch and change no other count, so a branch with no coloured output drains the name. | 1. For every list co of distinct coloured places, consumed input inp, list outs of distinct coloured outputs of the fired branch, consumed name s resident in inp and name marking M, and for every name u and coloured place i: the step's count of u at i, plus one if u is s and i is inp, equals M's count of u at i, plus one if u is s and i is in outs. | <pre>fun S ↦<br>  ∀ (co : List PlaceId),<br>    co.Nodup →<br>      ∀ (inp : PlaceId) (outs : List PlaceId) (s : ℕ) (M : Novel.RouteB.NM co),<br>        outs.Nodup →<br>          1 ≤ Novel.RouteB.cnt co M s inp →<br>            ∀ (u : ℕ) (i : Fin co.length),<br>              (S co inp outs s M u i + if u = s ∧ co[↑i] = inp then 1 else 0) =<br>                M u i + if u = s ∧ co[↑i] ∈ outs then 1 else 0</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The step is the name layer of Route B (`Novel.RouteB.NM`: the tokens of each name in each coloured place); which transition gets the coloured-consumer role is the block NU_051. The step is applied to a name resident in the consumed input (Route B's `will_fire` for a consumer), hence the premise that s has a token in inp, which the sentence states as 'with a name its coloured input holds'. Which resident name a consumer takes (any, on Route B; the oldest, FIFO, in the executor) is not this line's: it is the action contract and [NU-050]'s soundness; the outputs are the coloured places of the fired branch, without repetition (`colOut`), hence the premises on co and outs.
- The line is the quoted sentence, which restates 'A coloured consumer relays the consumed name-symbol into each coloured output of the fired branch (threading the same name), or drains it (dead-letters the name) on a branch that produces no coloured output'. A relay back into the consumed input leaves its count as it was, which the equation allows. That the name the action writes is the consumed one is the action contract (kind A, see NU_051): this line says what the name layer does, the contract is why that matches the executor ([NU-050], W9).
- AC6 (one `Xor` consumer relays on one branch and drains on another) is this line with outs the coloured outputs of each branch; NU_051_relay_nonvacuous applies it to one branch with a coloured output and one with none. The other acceptance criteria are the block NU_051's subject, which accounts for each.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): The Route B consumer step satisfies the relay line: it removes one token of `s` from the input (`removeAt_apply`, the name is resident) and adds one to each output (`foldl_add_apply`).
  <pre>NU_051_relay refConsumerStep</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_forbids_keepInput` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): ✗ A consumer step that does not take the name out of its input violates the relay line.
  <pre>¬NU_051_relay nu051_keepInput</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_forbids_remint` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): ✗ A consumer step that re-mints violates the relay line: relaying name `0` from `0` into `1` leaves no token of `0` in `1`.
  <pre>¬NU_051_relay nu051_remint</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_mutant_relayOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): The step that leaves the consumed token in its input kills the relay-only mutant: it adds one token of the name to each output (`foldl_add_apply`), so it meets the mutant reading, but the relay line asks the input to lose the token (`NU_051_relay_forbids_keepInput`).
  <pre>NU_051_relay_mutant_relayOnly nu051_keepInput ∧ ¬NU_051_relay nu051_keepInput</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): The relay line bites on the Route B step: name `0` is resident in place `0`; the branch that writes the coloured place `1` moves it there (relay), the branch with no coloured output leaves no token of it (drain), and no other name gains a token.
  <pre>1 ≤ Novel.RouteB.cnt [0, 1] nu051_M 0 0 ∧<br>  refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [1] 0 nu051_M 0 ⟨0, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>      0 ∧<br>    refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [1] 0 nu051_M 0 ⟨1, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>        1 ∧<br>      refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [] 0 nu051_M 0 ⟨0, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>          0 ∧<br>        refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [] 0 nu051_M 0<br>              ⟨1, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>            0 ∧<br>          refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [1] 0 nu051_M 1<br>              ⟨1, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>            0</pre>

## NU-052: Conflict-Only Priority for the Route B Name-SCG

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_052` · Kind **F** · Scope the Route B successor step, under CONFLICT and NONE · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `e364037334996d55`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* leave a base-enabled transition `L` unexpanded from a class exactly when another transition `H` of the net pre-empts `L` in that class, and *shall* expand every other base-enabled transition of the class as under `NONE`, in the same order.<br><br>*While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* take two transitions `H` and `L` whose input arcs on the places both consume from have cardinality `One` or `Exactly` to compete in a class exactly when some place is a consumed input of both and its token count in the class marking is less than the sum of the tokens each of them consumes from it on one firing.<br><br>*While* the mode is `NONE`, the Route B graph *shall* expand each base-enabled transition of a class, in the class's clock order (the code-point order of the transitions' names, [VER-010] AC1), with the successors the transition has when it is expanded alone from the same class and the same base layer, *shall* expand no other transition, and *shall not* read the readiness, in-flight state or competition of any transition.<br><br>*While* the mode is `NONE`, the Route B graph *shall* give a base-enabled transition at least one successor labelled with its name when the base layer can fire one of its branches in the class and the transition will fire on the name layer (always for an ordinary or minting transition, with an enabling name for a join, with a resident name for a consumer). | 1. Let E be the Route B expansion and C the competition test.<br>2. For every net whose transition names are distinct, every base layer whose competition is C read on the count marking κ of the class, and every class: the CONFLICT successors of the class are its NONE successors, in order, without those labelled with the name of a transition L of the net that some transition H of the net pre-empts in the class (glossary: Pre-empt, read as PreEmpts over the base layer's enabled, readyLe, idle and compete and the will-fire test of H's role).<br>3. For every count marking a and transitions H and L whose input arcs on the places both consume from have cardinality One or Exactly: C a H L holds exactly when some input arc of H is on a place that is also the place of an input arc of L and holds fewer tokens in a than the sum of the tokens H and L consume from it on one firing.<br>4. For every base layer, every class and every net whose transitions are listed in the code-point order of their names: the NONE successors of the class are, in that order, the NONE successors each base-enabled transition T has when the step is given T alone (the net [T]), from the same class and the same base layer.<br>5. For every two base layers that agree on enablement and firing: the NONE successors of every class are the same under both.<br>6. For every base layer, class and transition T that is base-enabled, has a branch the base layer fires in the class, and whose role will fire on the class's name layer (willFire): the NONE successors of the class in the net [T] include one labelled with T's name. | <pre>fun {β} E C ↦<br>  (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β) (κ : β → AMarking)<br>      (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role)<br>      (c : ℕ) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),<br>      (∀ (b : β), base.compete b = C (κ b)) →<br>        (List.map (fun T ↦ T.base.name) net).Nodup →<br>          E co base net role true c S =<br>            List.filter<br>              (fun x ↦<br>                !decide<br>                    (∃ L ∈ net, L.base.name = x.1 ∧ ∃ H ∈ net, PreEmpts base role S H L))<br>              (E co base net role false c S)) ∧<br>    (∀ (a : AMarking) (H L : Transition),<br>        (∀ s ∈ H.inputs ++ L.inputs,<br>            (∃ sh ∈ H.inputs, sh.place = s.place) →<br>              (∃ sl ∈ L.inputs, sl.place = s.place) → fixedCard s.card = true) →<br>          (C a H L = true ↔<br>            ∃ sh ∈ H.inputs,<br>              (∃ sl ∈ L.inputs, sl.place = sh.place) ∧<br>                a sh.place &lt;<br>                  Novel.RouteB.demandOn H sh.place + Novel.RouteB.demandOn L sh.place)) ∧<br>      (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)<br>          (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans)<br>          (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role) (c : ℕ)<br>          (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),<br>          List.Pairwise (fun T U ↦ T.base.name &lt; U.base.name) net →<br>            E co base net role false c S =<br>              List.flatMap (fun T ↦ E co base [T] role false c S)<br>                (List.filter (fun T ↦ base.enabled S.b T.base) net)) ∧<br>        (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base base' : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)<br>            (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans)<br>            (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role) (c : ℕ)<br>            (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),<br>            base'.enabled = base.enabled →<br>              base'.fire = base.fire →<br>                E co base' net role false c S = E co base net role false c S) ∧<br>          ∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)<br>            (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role)<br>            (c : ℕ) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β) (d : Novel.RouteB.Row),<br>            base.enabled S.b T.base = true →<br>              d ∈ T.rows →<br>                (base.fire S.b T.base d).isSome = true →<br>                  Novel.RouteB.willFire co (role T) S.m S.bound = true →<br>                    ∃ x ∈ E co base [T] role false c S, x.1 = T.base.name</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (E, C). E is one expansion of a class of the name-aware state-class graph of Route B ([VER-012]): the coloured set, the base layer (Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer: enabled, fire, readyLe, compete and idle), the net with its roles, the mode (true for CONFLICT, false for NONE), the mint counter and the class give the labelled successors, each labelled with the name of the transition that fired. The witness is refExpand, the shipped step Novel.RouteB.succ (name_state_class_graph.rs build_until). C is the competition test on a class's count marking; the witness is refCompete, Novel.RouteB.sharesConsumed (shares_consumed_input). The step reads competition through the base layer (as in Graph.lean), so line 1 is stated for the base layers whose compete is C read on the class's count marking κ; that is what makes C the graph's competition and not a separate function. The untimed base is such a layer, with κ the identity (nu052_untimedBase_compete). The timed base, whose count marking is the marking of the timed class, comes with wave W10; a base layer whose compete is not of this form is a wrong base layer, not a wrong graph, and is not this requirement's subject. The pruning predicate itself is the glossary term Pre-empt; its shipped form is refPrune (GlossaryNuVer, refPrune_iff).
- The first quoted sentence is line 1. 'Exactly when' restates the body's 'is not expanded from a class when' together with the soundness paragraph's 'The pruning removes only interleavings in which a lower-priority transition fires ahead of a ready, conflicting, strictly-higher-priority one': under CONFLICT the graph prunes and does nothing else. 'Another transition' is read as another name: the line is stated for nets whose transition names are distinct, because the shipped step labels successors with names and compares H and L by name (name_state_class_graph.rs:587, `h.name() != l.name()`). Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10, with D23 settling that distinct names are one shared assumption for every name-keyed requirement), so the premise is that assumption and the quoted sentence needs no narrowing. Outside it, on a net where two transitions share a name, the Rust prune never lets one pre-empt the other, while the Java and TypeScript prunes compare by identity (NameStateClassGraph.java:402, name-state-class-graph.ts:336) and do; D10 puts that net out of scope, so the case is not encoded.
- Line 1 reads every bullet of the body through the glossary term Pre-empt: strictly higher priority, competition (the base layer's compete, line 2 on count markings), ready no later than L (the base layer's readyLe), no firing in flight (the base layer's idle) and 'actually fires in this class' (willFire of H's role: a join needs an enabling name, a consumer a resident one, so a name-disabled join pre-empts nothing). H ranges over the base-enabled transitions of the class, as the body's 'another enabled transition H in the same class'. 'Actually fires in this class' is read on the name layer, as the body's own gloss ('a name-disabled join, whose inputs carry no shared name, produces no name-successor') and the shipped prune (dominated reads will_fire and no firing of the base) do; whether H has a branch the base layer can fire is not part of it. On the untimed base every enabled transition fires. On a timed base, H ready no later than L (readyLe) makes H firable whenever L is, and when L is not firable pruning it removes no successor; that this holds of the timed readyLe is the timed base's subject (wave W10).
- The second quoted sentence is line 2, stated for transitions whose input arcs on the places both consume from have cardinality One or Exactly (fixedCard). An All or AtLeast arc on a place only one of them consumes from plays no part in the demand on a shared place, so the premise leaves it free and line 2 still constrains such a pair (NU_052_forbids_wholePair). The body defines a demand as 'the tokens that transition consumes from p on one firing'; the runtimes and the Lean model use the required count (consumed_demand, Card.required), which is 1 for All and n for AtLeast(n), not the tokens consumed. For One and Exactly the two agree, so line 2 uses demandOn under that premise. Which reading holds for All and AtLeast on a shared place is ruling D97 (clash nu-c#3), and the widened line waits for it (wave W10); until then the quoted sentence names One and Exactly. 'Read and inhibitor arcs do not count' is line 2's 'consumed input of both': only input arcs occur in it.
- The body's 'becomes ready no later than L by the class-relative residual earliest: the DBM lower bound of each enabled clock captured before time is let to pass (readyEarliest, parallel to the enabled set)', the comparison within a float epsilon, and the sentence '*While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* take `H` to be ready no later than `L` in a class exactly when `readyEarliest[H] <= readyEarliest[L]` within a float epsilon, where `readyEarliest` is the DBM lower bound of each enabled clock before time is let to pass.' are a timing line over a timed base layer, as are the body's claims that a static H.earliest() <= L.earliest() does not suffice, that the rule subsumes the immediate-H case and that it also prunes sound non-zero-earliest conflicts. The base layer here is abstract (readyLe); its timed instance needs the timed class of RefScg (VER-010), so this sentence is not encoded here and comes with wave W10. On the untimed base every transition is ready at once (untimedBase.readyLe is true).
- The third quoted sentence is lines 3 and 4. It restates 'The default mode, NONE, MUST reproduce the prior Route B behaviour byte-for-byte' with the first paragraph's 'it expands every base-enabled transition': line 3 says no transition's NONE successors depend on another transition, that they come in the class's clock order and that a transition not base-enabled adds none, so NONE prunes nothing by priority; line 4 says NONE reads none of the base layer's readyLe, idle and compete, the inputs only the prune reads.
- 'In the class's clock order': the runtimes walk a class's enabled transitions in the class's canonical clock order, ascending transition name in code-point order ([VER-010] AC1; the Rust, Java and TypeScript name-state-class graphs walk the base class's enabled list, which the state-class graph permutes into canonical order when it builds a class). The model's step walks the net list it is given, so line 3 is stated for a net listed in that order (the Pairwise premise), and the model's list order is then the runtimes' order on every class. A net listed in another order is the same net handed to the step in another enumeration; line 1's 'in the same order' compares CONFLICT with NONE on one enumeration and needs no premise.
- 'Expanded alone from the same class and the same base layer' is the net [T] with the class and the base layer unchanged. The base layer is the class's own: the base successor of T is computed over the whole net (its clocks, enabled set and readyEarliest, state_class_graph.rs compute_successor_gated), and in the model that whole-net computation is inside base.fire, which line 3 does not vary, so [T] is not the net holding T alone. The minted symbols are compared up to the canonical key of the class ([VER-012] AC2): the runtimes thread one mint counter across the expansions of a class and across classes (name_state_class_graph.rs next_sym), while line 3 passes the same counter c to every transition, so the raw symbol numbers of the runtimes agree with the model only after interning.
- The fourth quoted sentence is line 5. It is the least that 'expands' says of one transition: a transition that fires on both layers yields a successor labelled with its name, so an expansion that yields nothing is ruled out (NU_052_forbids_empty). The will-fire condition is the body's name-disabled join, which 'produces no name-successor', read the other way. Which successors one transition yields, all of them and byte for byte, is VER-012's subject, cited in wave W10, so 'the prior Route B behaviour' is not stated as a fixed function here.
- Which mode the verifier hands the step is outside the step. On a net with a reapable transition Route B does not prune ([VER-002], 'It does not prune by priority ([NU-052]) on a net with a reapable transition.'; nu_scg_verifier.rs:195-200 turns CONFLICT into NONE). NU-052's body states the pruning without that exception; whether NU-052 gains the sentence is ruling D97 (clash nu-c#4). The lines here hold for whatever mode the step is given, so they need neither answer.
- The paragraph 'In-flight actions' (the split rule: a verifier MUST split every pruner and every transition depositing into an input or read place of a pruner on a net with a ν-join, MUST NOT let H pre-empt while inflight:<H> is marked, falls back to the NONE verdict naming the transition when one cannot be split, keeps the pruning under assumeAtomicFiring and on a direct call to Route B) is a pipeline obligation over the split net. It needs RefSplit (VER-004) and the pipeline slice of RefVerifier, and its scope (a net with a ν-join) waits for ruling D97; it comes with wave W10. What this block keeps of it is the in-flight guard as the base layer's idle in line 1; that idle is the count of inflight:<H> being 0 is the split model's subject.
- The paragraph 'Soundness' (the pruned firings are ones the eager, priority-ordered executor never performs; L is re-examined after H fires) relates the graph to the executor. It needs RefExec with a priority-ordered pass and actions in flight, and it must list EXEC-003 AC4 (a ν-join that received a same-pass deposit fires no earlier than the next cycle). Whether the Java and TypeScript wording of the in-flight case stays is ruling D8. It comes with wave W10; Libpetri.postFixPrune_agrees_with_executor (Priority.lean) is true by construction and is no evidence for it.
- The option names prioritySemantics / priority_semantics, that CONFLICT is opt-in and that an implementation MAY omit it are configuration, not encoded.
- AC1 (NONE is the default and the only mode an implementation MUST provide; NONE leaves every existing Route B verdict unchanged) is lines 3, 4 and 5 for the step: NONE expands each base-enabled transition on its own, reads nothing the prune reads and gives every transition that fires a successor. The default and the verdicts are configuration and VER-012's graph; not encoded beyond that.
- AC2 (the fork-threaded co-mint plus immediate ν-join plus delayed lower-priority drain fixture: Violated under NONE, Proven under CONFLICT on Route B called directly and under assumeAtomicFiring; through verify() with the split on, the NONE verdict and a report note) needs the timed base (a delayed drain), the verdict and the pipeline; it comes with wave W10. Its step-level core, that under CONFLICT the join's competitor is pruned when the join pre-empts it, is line 1 (NU_052_nonvacuous on the untimed base).
- AC3 (no over-pruning: a genuine orphan, whose join is name-disabled, still reaches its drain) is line 1's will-fire condition. The Route B retrodiction of commit c23cd9e (Novel.RouteB.WF: a priority-10 join whose keys hold two different names and a priority-0 drain competing for one token) is the evidence: the pre-fix prune without the will-fire guard stalls the class (NU_052_forbids_preFix), and the shipped step keeps the drain's edge (NU_052_orphan_not_pruned). The verdicts Violated without a drain and Proven with one are VER-012's graph and come with wave W10.
- AC4 (only consumed-input conflicts prune; a read or inhibitor arc on the shared place creates no conflict) is line 2 (NU_052_forbids_reads, NU_052_nonvacuous).
- AC5 (a delayed(100) ν-join still pre-empts a delayed(200) lower-priority drain, so DEADLETTER is unreachable under CONFLICT and reachable under NONE) is the residual-earliest comparison over a timed base and a verdict; it comes with wave W10. Line 1 keeps the readiness condition (NU_052_forbids_noReady).
- AC6 (when the shared consumed place holds enough tokens for both transitions, CONFLICT does not prune the lower-priority one) is line 2 (NU_052_forbids_noCount) and, on the step, NU_052_nonvacuous (two tokens: both expanded).
- AC7 (a pruner in flight pre-empts nothing: H with an asynchronous action, L, the refill g, Unreachable(bad) Violated under CONFLICT with L in the trace) needs the split net (inflight:<H>) and the verdict; it comes with wave W10. Line 1 keeps the in-flight condition as the base layer's idle (NU_052_forbids_noIdle); the count-level witness is Libpetri.inFlight_guard_is_necessary (Priority.lean).
- The test derivation (the ν-join versus timed dead-letter drain fixture, the genuine orphan, every verdict attributed to Route B) is AC2 and AC3 and comes with wave W10.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_055"></a>
## NU-055: Name Alignment

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_055` · Kind **F** · Scope every verifier that offers NameAligned or QuiescentNameAligned (MAY); the predicate on a class of the Route B graph · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `629605d1633d5a53`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| For places `p` and `q` of `S`, the same place included, and the name-symbols `s` and `t`: `s` resident in `p` and `t` resident in `q` imply `s = t`.<br><br>An empty place imposes nothing, but a place holding two names violates it whatever the others hold, so the singleton `NameAligned(p)` says that `p` never holds two names.<br><br>*Where* name alignment is offered, `NameAligned(S)` for a non-empty `S` *shall* hold on a class of the graph exactly when, for places `p` and `q` of `S`, the same place included, every name-symbol resident in `p` equals every name-symbol resident in `q`.<br><br>The predicate compares names only for equality, so it is invariant under any permutation of the name-symbols.<br><br>It is therefore a function of the canonical key of a class ([VER-012] AC2), and deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph.<br><br>Its places compare by name, and a place listed twice counts once, at its first occurrence, so `NameAligned(box, list, box)` is `NameAligned(box, list)`.<br><br>The order of `S` changes no verdict; it fixes the description and which place a reason names. | 1. For every coloured set co, base type β, non-empty list ps and class S of the graph, the check A answers true exactly when any name-symbol s resident in a place p of ps and any name-symbol t resident in a place q of ps, p = q allowed, are equal. | <pre>fun A ↦<br>  ∀ (co : List PlaceId) (β : Type) (ps : List PlaceId) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),<br>    ps ≠ [] →<br>      (A co β ps S = true ↔<br>        ∀ p ∈ ps,<br>          ∀ q ∈ ps,<br>            ∀ (s t : ℕ),<br>              Novel.RouteB.resident co p S.m s = true →<br>                Novel.RouteB.resident co q S.m t = true → s = t)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a class of the Route B graph (NState co β, Graph.lean): a base b, a name layer m giving each name-symbol and each coloured place (a position of co) a count, and a bound above every live symbol. A name-symbol s is resident in p when its count there is not 0 (Name.lean resident). The NameAligned bullet speaks of a marking; its EARS restatement and the line speak of a class of the graph, which is where Route B evaluates the predicate. A marking's names are read on its coloured places through the one projection nameOf: its class is its name view (view co nameOf m), and on that view the line is the statement that all tokens in the places of S carry one name (alignedAll_view_iff, cited). Places are PlaceId, so 'its places compare by name' is equality of ids, and the check takes S as a list.
- The line is the definition of the NameAligned bullet (its second and third sentences, restated by the EARS sentence): self pairs included, so a place holding two names fails whatever the others hold, and an empty place has no resident symbol and imposes nothing. The QuiescentNameAligned bullet reads 'the same predicate'; where it is read is NU_055_sound's subject. The first sentence of the NameAligned bullet ('in every reachable marking') is NU_055_sound's.
- The permutation sentence, the first half of the canonical-key sentence and the S-order sentences ('a place listed twice counts once', 'The order of S changes no verdict', read on the predicate) are consequences of the line, not lines of their own: the line fixes A on every non-empty list, so A is the shipped check there (NU_055_eq_ref), and NU_055_perm, NU_055_key and NU_055_members derive the three invariances. The spec states them with 'so' and 'therefore', and they get no EARS sentence. The models that break one of them (nu055_symZero, nu055_headOnly) are killed by the line itself. The second half of the canonical-key sentence ('deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph') is also a claim about the verdict: the verdict on a closed graph is the predicate's answer over its classes, NU_055_truncation line 3.
- An uncoloured place has no row in the name layer, so nothing is resident there (resident_of_not_mem) and the line holds vacuously for it (alignedAll_uncoloured, cited). That such a place is refused (refusal step 6, 'Coloured places only', AC2) is not a line of this block. It is the later refusal line of this ID, item (4) of the design row in design/nu.md and 'NU-055 line 4' in the plan's W0 Defers, a different thing from any line here: the refusal steps need the pipeline slice of the verifier model (wave W10) and the wording rulings under D20 (clashes nu-c#9, NC-7). The design's mutant 'proves on an uncoloured place' moves with that line.
- 'A place listed twice counts once, at its first occurrence' also fixes the description and which place a reason names, and 'The order of S changes no verdict' also covers the reason of an Unknown. The description (the Property: line) is N (an API note), and which place a reason names is the refusal order's (wave W10, D20). On the predicate, the only part of the verdict this block models, order and repeats change nothing (NU_055_members).
- 'An empty S MUST be rejected where it is constructed' and 'S is a non-empty list' are the language API (N): each constructor rejects an empty list (Java records, the TypeScript signature, the Rust panic, the Python ValueError). The line is stated for a non-empty S only, so the block fixes no answer for the empty list, which never reaches a verdict.
- AC5 (invariance under name permutation, on a class and that class permuted, and under reordering S) is NU_055_perm and NU_055_members, theorems of the line; its run of the worked example with names minted in another scope ([NU-010]) is a test of the minter (NU-010, NU-011, wave W9) and of the verdict, not of the predicate, and is not encoded.
- AC7 ('S is a list'; the cross pair of reply and staged without the self pairs would accept a marking with two stale replies in reply) is the line with self pairs: NU_055_forbids_crossOnly kills the check without self pairs. AC7's construction rules are the API (N, above) and NU_055_members; its descriptions are N; its verdicts and witness lengths on the worked example are tests on the fixtures (Q), as the Route B graph of that net is not computed in Lean.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): The shipped check satisfies NU-055: `alignedAll` is the pairwise reading with self pairs (`alignedAll_eq_true_iff`, `aligned_eq_true_iff`).
  <pre>NU_055 refAlignCheck</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_forbids_crossOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): ✗ The cross pairs alone violate NU-055: on the singleton `[0]` the check accepts place `0` holding the names `0` and `1`, which the line refuses (AC7: a place holding two names violates the predicate whatever the others hold).
  <pre>¬NU_055 nu055_crossOnly</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_forbids_headOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): ✗ Reading only the first place violates NU-055: on `nu055_mixed` the check accepts `[0, 1]` because place `0` holds one name, while place `1` holds two and the line refuses the list. The line kills it directly; the same model also breaks the members consequence (`[1, 0]` is refused).
  <pre>¬NU_055 nu055_headOnly</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_forbids_symZero` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): ✗ Comparing names with a fixed name violates NU-055: place `0` holding the one name `1` is aligned on `[0]`, and the check refuses it. The line kills it directly; the same model also breaks the permutation and key consequences (`nu055_zero` is accepted, its swap `nu055_one`, with the same key, is not).
  <pre>¬NU_055 nu055_symZero</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_mutant_crossOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): The cross-pairs check kills the mutant reading without self pairs: it is that reading, so it meets it, but NU-055, whose line includes the self pairs, rejects it on a place holding two names (`NU_055_forbids_crossOnly`, AC7).
  <pre>NU_055_mutant_crossOnly nu055_crossOnly ∧ ¬NU_055 nu055_crossOnly</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): The line of NU-055 is exercised by the shipped check, on both sides of its `iff`: places `0` and `1` holding the one name `0` are aligned, and so is the singleton `[0]` there (two places and self pairs); place `0` holding two names is not aligned on `[0]` (a place holding two names) nor on `[1, 0]` (whatever the others hold); place `1` empty imposes nothing on `[1]`. The consequences show on the same examples: the class with the names swapped gives the same answer (NU_055_perm, NU_055_key), and `[0, 1]` and `[1, 0, 1]` give the same answer on the mixed class (NU_055_members).
  <pre>refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0, 1] nu055_same = true ∧<br>  refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0] nu055_same = true ∧<br>    refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0] nu055_two = false ∧<br>      refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [1, 0] nu055_two = false ∧<br>        refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [1] nu055_two = true ∧<br>          refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0] nu055_zero =<br>              refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0] nu055_one ∧<br>            refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0, 1] nu055_mixed = false ∧<br>              refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [1, 0, 1] nu055_mixed = false</pre>
