**Assumptions**

- A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic: the step that starts a firing completes it. Armed, Mid (the intermediate marking: inputs consumed, reset places drained, nothing deposited) and Enabled are the glossary terms.
- The intermediate marking is computed from the marking of the state the firing step starts from, which is the live marking (ruling D7, revised). In a firing pass of several firings each firing is its own atomic step, so a token a synchronous action deposited earlier in the pass is in that marking and counts, as the section says. This agrees with a pass only for arcs that take a fixed number of tokens: a draining arc (reset, all(), atLeast(n)) later in a pass takes only the tokens present when the pass began ([EXEC-003] AC5), while Mid drains the live place. The section's bullet on reset places now carries the exception for this case (ruling 2): a same-pass deposit that the reset does not take ([EXEC-003] AC5) and that keeps the transition enabled in the intermediate marking keeps its clock. The Phase 1 relation has no pass, so a same-pass deposit never arises in it, and Mid draining the whole live place is the bullet without its exception; the exception, and an intermediate marking that keeps a deposit the reset does not take, are deferred to Phase 2 (RefExec). Outputs of an asynchronous action still in flight do not exist in the Phase 1 relation, which has no asynchronous actions. The enablement recheck of the pass ([EXEC-003] AC3-AC5) is not part of this block; see the next line. A synchronous action does not hide the gap: in the atomic Phase 1 step its deposit is the step's deposit d, which Mid t s.m never sees, so line 1 applies to a refill by the firing's own outputs (AC1). The asynchronous half is AC5, deferred below.
- The fifth 'shall' sentence, 'If the enablement recheck of a firing pass finds a transition disabled ([EXEC-003] AC3), then the transition shall lose its clock, even when a same-pass deposit keeps it enabled in the live marking.', and the body's sentences on it (a transition the recheck finds disabled is disarmed even when a same-pass deposit refilled its place, and is newly armed, with a fresh stamp, by a later enablement update that finds it enabled) are not encoded and not quoted (ruling 1). The recheck judges a transition on the marking of the pass, which the atomic Phase 1 relation does not have: each firing is its own step and sees the live marking. Deferred to Phase 2 (RefExec), with the order of the two rules inside one pass: the intermediate-marking rule is applied at each firing on the live marking, and the recheck afterwards on the pass's marking, so a transition can keep its stamp through a firing by sentence 2 and then lose its clock to the recheck later in the same pass. The two rules are applied in sequence, they do not contradict each other.
- To lose a clock is to hold no stamp after the firing. Sentences 1 and 4 together are line 1 of the formula: an armed transition other than t that is not enabled in the intermediate marking holds no stamp after the firing, unless it is enabled after it, in which case it is newly armed, that is armed with the current reading of the firing clock ([TIME-010]). Sentences 3 and 4 together are line 3, for the fired transition itself; it presupposes, as sentence 4 does, a clock to lose, so it speaks of the transition armed before the firing. An unarmed transition does not fire ([TIME-010] line 5). Line 2 is sentence 2. An armed transition enabled in the intermediate marking but not after the firing is disabled by the firing's deposit; that case is [TIME-011], not this block.
- Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10): 'other than t' is 'named differently from t', and lines 1-3 speak of the transition the net holds under the name (InNet). Line 3 picks it by t's name, so a fired t that is not the net's transition of its name (a foreign or duplicate-named t) still restarts the clock under that name. The section assumes pairwise distinct names (NamesDistinct), under which InNet is membership in the net.
- Bullet 1 (removing tokens never disables through an inhibitor arc) is time012_inhibitor_never: a transition enabled before whose input and read arcs still hold in the intermediate marking is enabled there. Its ν-join clause is not encoded: the Phase 1 relation has no ν correlation, it belongs to the NU blocks.
- Bullet 2 (a reset arc drains its place) is time012_reset_disables, read as an input arc with a positive required count or a read arc on a reset place of t; with line 1 such a transition restarts its clock. Its exception for a same-pass deposit the reset does not take is Phase 2, as said above. An input arc whose required count is 0 stays enabled in a drained place and keeps its clock (the time012_Tzero conjuncts of TIME_012_ac3). Bullet 3 (surplus tokens keep the clock) is AC4. Bullet 4 (the fired transition always starts a fresh clock) is line 3.
- AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 are the examples TIME_012_ac1 (input refill), TIME_012_ac2 (read only), TIME_012_ac3 (reset drain with a positive requirement) and TIME_012_ac4 (surplus keeps), in milliseconds, with T Delayed(5) and the refresh transition Immediate. TIME-012 fixes only the stamp a firing leaves; AC1's lower bound (T fires no earlier than d after the refill) follows from TIME-012 together with [TIME-010] lines 2 and 4, which frame the stamps across the other steps and gate the firing. TIME_012_ac1 shows the bound for the reference step: T does not fire 4 ms after the refill. AC5 (an asynchronous action) and AC6 (TransitionClockRestarted or TransitionEnabled) need in-flight actions and the event log, and are deferred to the Phase 2 executor; AC4's event clause (no TransitionClockRestarted or TransitionEnabled for T) needs the event log and is deferred with AC6. The state class graph's persistence rule ([VER-010]) is in Novel/TimedScg/Run.lean: persistence_rule, fired_never_persists, reset_restarts and surplus_keeps cite this ID.
- A firing is instantaneous on the firing clock: that frame is not a sentence of this section and is not in the statement. Without it a firing fused with a hidden delay satisfies TIME-012 (TIME_012_gap_fireAdvancesClock); the frame is time012_FramesClock, which the reference satisfies (TIME_012_reference_framesClock) and which ConsistencyTime conjoins.
- Injected tokens are not steps of the Phase 1 relation, which has no environment places, so injection plays no part here.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-TIME_013"></a>
## TIME-013: Deadline Enforcement

`Libpetri.Spec.TIME_013` · Kind **T** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/03-timing.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `cf60477e972fe310`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| When a reapable transition is expired, that is, armed with an elapsed time strictly greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, the executor reaps it: it disarms the transition without firing it and emits a `TransitionTimedOut` event.<br><br>Implementations MUST apply a deadline tolerance — a grace band beyond `latest` (default 5ms) that absorbs timer-resolution and scheduling jitter — and SHOULD expose it as a configurable per-executor option (e.g. `deadlineTolerance` / `deadline_tolerance_ms`); a value of `0` gives strict enforcement.<br><br>Only `Deadline` and `Window` transitions are reaped here.<br><br>*If* a reapable transition's elapsed time is greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, *then* the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>The executor *shall not* reap a transition that is not reapable.<br><br>*While* a transition is reaped, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*If* a reapable transition is armed and its elapsed time is greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance, *then* the executor *shall* reap it in the deadline step of that cycle ([EXEC-001] step 4) and emit `TransitionTimedOut` ([EVT-009]).<br><br>*When* a firing or an injected token writes one of a reaped transition's arc places (an input, read, inhibitor or reset place) and the transition is enabled afterwards, the transition *shall* be newly armed with a fresh clock ([TIME-010]).<br><br>A firing writes a place when it consumes from it, deposits into it or drains it through a reset arc; draining a reset place that is already empty counts as a write.<br><br>A reaped transition keeps its input tokens and is not armed again until one of its arc places is written, so an executor that fell behind can come to rest at a marking that still enables it. | 1. For every timed net X:<br>2. a reap of u is of a transition of the net, is taken only from a state in which u is expired, and leaves u reaped, the marking, the reading of the firing clock and the stamp of every other name as they were;<br>3. no transition fires from a state in which it is reapable and its elapsed time is greater than its latest bound plus the tolerance;<br>4. no transition is reaped from a state in which it is not reapable;<br>5. no transition fires from a state in which it is reaped;<br>6. a step that leaves the net's transition u reaped, from a state in which u is armed, is a reap of a transition of u's name;<br>7. a step that leaves the net's transition u armed, from a state in which u is reaped, is a firing that writes one of u's arc places;<br>8. a firing that writes an arc place of the net's transition u, from a state in which u is reaped, leaves u armed with the reading of the firing clock if u is enabled after it;<br>9. a firing is of a transition of the net;<br>10. from every state in which a transition of the net is expired, the step relation has a reap of it. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (X : TimedNet N),<br>    (∀ (u : Reference.Trans N),<br>        on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.reap u) s', shall fun s s' ↦<br>          u ∈ X.net.transitions ∧<br>            Expired X s u ∧<br>              Reaped s' u ∧<br>                s'.m = s.m ∧<br>                  ClockReading s' = ClockReading s ∧<br>                    ∀ (n : String), n ≠ u.core.name → s'.stamp n = s.stamp n) ∧<br>      (∀ (u : Reference.Trans N),<br>          while fun s ↦ Reapable X u ∧ (TimingOf X u).latest + Tolerance X &lt; **Assumptions**

- A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic. Reapable, Expired, Reaped, Armed, Elapsed time, Arc place and Write are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean); Reaped is the state reading, enabled at the marking and not armed.
- Line 1 reads the section's first paragraph as the definition of a reap step: it is taken only from an expired transition (reapable, armed, elapsed time strictly greater than its latest bound plus the tolerance, ruling D4), so the tolerance is applied, and it disarms that transition and nothing else, without firing it: the marking ("keeps its input tokens"), the clock reading and every other stamp stay. Several reaps in one deadline step are several reap steps.
- Line 9 is the 'shall' sentence on reaping, and the first quoted sentence's 'the executor reaps it', as far as one atomic step can state them: from every state in which a transition of the net is expired, a reap of it is a step (the same condition as CoversReap, for this block; TIME-003 and TIME-005 state it for their timings). The step relation has no cycles and no events, so that the reap is taken, in the deadline step of the very cycle ([EXEC-001] step 4), and emits TransitionTimedOut ([EVT-009]) are deferred to Phase 2 and EVT. The atomic relation also lets another transition fire while u is expired (RefTStep does), and that firing may restart u's clock under [TIME-012], which a real cycle cannot do because its deadline step reaps before its firing pass; ClashesTime records this as a Phase 2 obligation (clash013_refresh_rescue).
- The tolerance is the field TimedNet.tol, any natural number of milliseconds; the statement holds for every tolerance. Its default of 5 ms, the value 0 for strict enforcement and its exposure as a per-executor option (AC2) are configuration (kind N) and are not encoded.
- Line 5 ties the state reading Reaped to the act of reaping: an armed transition becomes enabled and unarmed only by a reap of it, so a delay or a firing that silently drops the clock of an enabled transition is not a reap. Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10, InNet): the section assumes pairwise distinct names (NamesDistinct), and the reap of line 5 is of a transition of u's name.
- Lines 1 and 8 make the transition of a reap or a firing label one of the net's. Without them a label outside the net that shares a name with a net transition but has another timing could reap or fire under that name, and lines 1 to 4 would check the label's timing, not the net's. Under distinct names a label of the net with u's name is u itself (time013_label_eq), so lines 1 to 5 speak of the net's transition (TIME_013_reap_is_of_u). Nets with two transitions of one name are outside ruling D10: the reference step itself then shares one stamp between them, so the statement does not speak to them.
- Line 3 follows from line 1, as Expired includes Reapable (time013_line3_of_line1); it is kept so the quoted sentence on not reaping a non-reapable transition maps to one line.
- Lines 6 and 7 are TIME-010's lines 1 and 3 read for a reaped transition (with line 1's fresh stamp in line 7), and are proven from the same policy-generic lemmas. A write is the glossary's Write (ruling D6): any arc place, not only an input place, and draining an empty reset place counts. The injected-token case of the last quoted 'shall' sentence is outside the step relation: injection is not a step of the Phase 1 relation, which has no environment places.
- AC1 (a Deadline(5s) transition still armed past 5 s plus the tolerance does not fire after that bound; if it is still armed on the first cycle whose elapsed time is strictly greater than the bound, it is reaped in that cycle and TransitionTimedOut is emitted) is the nonvacuous example TIME_013_nonvacuous in milliseconds with tolerance 5: not reaped at elapsed 5005, reaped at 5006, and not fireable then. That the reap falls in the first such cycle is the cycle loop of Phase 2 (RefExec, [EXEC-001] step 4), and the TransitionTimedOut event is [EVT-009], deferred with it. AC3 (an Exact transition past its target is not disabled) is the same example: the Exact(3) transition, at elapsed 5006, cannot be reaped and fires. AC4 (a reaped transition does not fire until an arc place is written, then is armed again with a fresh clock and may fire) is the same example after the reap, ending with a firing of the re-armed transition; the backends (Bitmap, Precompiled) are Phase 2.
- The paragraph on verification (quiescence reads a marking whose enabled transitions are all reapable as quiescent, Route B drops the latest bounds, assumeNoReaping) belongs to [VER-002], [VER-004] and [VER-012]; it is cited by ReapAware.rest_sound, not encoded here.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-TIME_015"></a>
## TIME-015: Injectable Clock

`Libpetri.Spec.TIME_015` · Kind **A** · Scope all executors, on the default or an injected firing clock · Source **verbatim** (spec/03-timing.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `1fe98378e952e8b1`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* an executor runs on an injected clock, successive readings of its firing clock *shall* be non-decreasing.<br><br>*When* the executor's wait completes, the executor *shall* re-check its boundary conditions before it fires any transition, so an armed transition *shall not* fire before its earliest bound because a wait completed early ([TIME-010]). | 1. For every timed net X:<br>2. no step lowers the reading of the firing clock;<br>3. a delay of δ advances the reading by exactly δ;<br>4. no transition fires from the state a delay of any length reached if, read with the stamps held before the delay, it is armed there and its elapsed time is below its earliest bound;<br>5. no transition fires from the state a delay of any length reached if, read with the stamps held before the delay, it is expired there. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (X : TimedNet N),<br>    (∀ (l : TLbl N),<br>        on fun s s' ↦ R X s l s', shall fun s s' ↦ ClockReading s ≤ ClockReading s') ∧<br>      (∀ (δ : ℕ),<br>          on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.delay δ) s', shall fun s s' ↦<br>            ClockReading s' = ClockReading s + δ) ∧<br>        (∀ (δ : ℕ) (u : Reference.Trans N),<br>            on fun s₀ s ↦ R X s₀ (TLbl.delay δ) s, shall fun s₀ s ↦<br>              Armed (AfterWait s₀ s) u →<br>                Elapsed (AfterWait s₀ s) u &lt; (TimingOf X u).earliest →<br>                  ∀ (d : List N) (s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧<br>          ∀ (δ : ℕ) (u : Reference.Trans N),<br>            on fun s₀ s ↦ R X s₀ (TLbl.delay δ) s, shall fun s₀ s ↦<br>              Expired X (AfterWait s₀ s) u →<br>                ∀ (d : List N) (s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock (ClockReading) and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). The relation has one firing clock and does not say where its readings come from, so the block holds of the default clock as of an injected one. The epoch clock (token creation times, [CORE-011]) is not modelled: the Phase 1 marking is token counts. Injected tokens are not steps of the Phase 1 relation.
- Line 1 of the formula is the first 'shall' sentence, over every step. A host reading that goes backwards cannot be written as a delay, since a delay's length is a natural number: across a wait, the sentence is carried by that type together with line 2, and a clock that rewinds on a delay breaks lines 1 and 2 at once (TIME_015_forbids_rewind). Line 1 on its own constrains firings and reaps: one that lowers the reading breaks it alone (TIME_015_mutant_waitOnly_killed).
- Line 2 says a delay moves the clock by its length; it is the only statement of that fact, and TIME-003 to TIME-006 rely on it through ConsistencyTime for the elapsed time of their transitions to grow with the clock (their clock frame keeps the stamp across a delay, GlossaryTime ClockFrame). That a firing and a reap take no time (an atomic step happens at one reading) is a convention of the Phase 1 relation, not a sentence of this section, so it is not a line of this block; its firing half is time012_FramesClock, which ConsistencyTime conjoins, and its reap half is [TIME-013] line 1 (a reap leaves the clock reading as it is). Which reading stamps a transition armed by a firing is not fixed by the spec text and is open: the model takes the firing step's own reading (refPolicy.fresh), while a runtime that samples the clock once per cycle stamps it with the reading of the next cycle's enablement update, and an asynchronous action's outputs arm at its completion reading ([TIME-012] AC5, deferred).
- Contract 1's other half (the clock is not assumed to advance between two reads) is not a line of this block. A repeated reading is a delay of 0; that one is offered is CoversDelay, and that it changes nothing else is TIME-010's framing of stamps across a delay together with FramesMarking. The reference meets it (time015_stutter).
- Lines 3 and 4 are the second 'shall' sentence. A completed wait is a delay step of any length: the executor cannot tell an early or spurious completion from a due one, so both lines quantify over every delay. The boundary conditions are read in AfterWait: the marking and reading after the wait with the stamps held before it, so that a wait that rewrites or drops stamps cannot hide an early firing (TIME_015_mutant_inState_killed, TIME_015_forbids_dropStamps). For a relation that keeps stamps across a delay, as TIME-010 line 2 asks, AfterWait is the state the wait reached.
- Line 3 is the earliest side, which the sentence names. Line 4 is the latest side of 'its boundary conditions': a transition that is expired (glossary: reapable, armed, elapsed time strictly greater than its latest bound plus the deadline tolerance; rulings D2 and D4) does not fire after a wait that overshot. Exact transitions are not reapable and are never expired [TIME-006]. With TIME-010 and FramesMarking, line 3 holds of every relation (time015_ac4_of_time010, cited for AC4).
- AC6: the reap test, that with tolerance 0 a Deadline transition can be reaped exactly when it is armed and its elapsed time is strictly greater than its bound, is the cited theorem time015_ac6_reap_strict (the strict test of TIME-013, ruling D4). That the reap happens on the first such cycle is a property of the executor loop and is deferred to Phase 2.
- AC10 is not encoded: its ruling (D12) is open. The clash is recorded, and cited for TIME-015, with the other TIME clashes (ClashesTime.lean): if its 'same outcome' quantifies over strictly increasing clocks that may skip a window, the reference refutes it (time015_ac10_coarse_jump: a Window(3, 5) transition with tolerance 0 fires under a clock advancing 1 ms per reading, and is reaped, its token stranded, under the readings 0 then 10); repeated readings alone change nothing (refTStepW_delay_zero: a delay of 0 is an identity step; time015_stutter here is the converse, that such a step exists).
- AC1, AC2, AC3, AC9, AC12, AC14 and AC15 are properties of the seam, its default path, its documentation and its identifiers (configuration, N kind), not of a step relation. AC5, AC7, AC8 and AC11 are properties of the executor loop (abort, the boundary short-circuit, wake-up, reentrant admission) and AC13 of token stamping through the epoch clock; they are deferred to Phase 2.

## VER-025: Bounded Witness Phase

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_025` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-10 104625b4eefcf18b** · Statement hash `104625b4eefcf18b`

| *If* the pipeline reaches the flat fixpoint query, the witness depth `D` is positive, and the net has no match transitions or the property is a reachability-safety property with a budget place declared, *then* the verifier *shall* run the phase directly before the fixpoint script is encoded.<br><br>*While* the fixpoint query takes the name-coloured encoding ([NU-053]), the verifier *shall not* run the phase.<br><br>*If* the net has match transitions and either the property is not a reachability-safety property or no budget place is declared, *then* the verifier *shall not* run the injection step, and any other value, or a selector the model leaves undefined, as idle, and *shall* read no run from a model that defines no selector.<br><br>*When* the phase replays a run, it *shall* fire each transition step under the exact abstract semantics with the environment post-caps, take each injection step only while its guard holds, and accept the run only when every step is enabled and the last marking violates the property.<br><br>*When* a run replays, the phase *shall* trim it: it *shall* first cut the run to its violating prefix, then try the steps from the last to the first, replace the run by the violating prefix of the run without that step whenever one exists, and repeat such passes until one changes nothing.<br><br>*When* the phase reports a run, it *shall* report the trimmed run, replayed, with each transition step labelled by its transition's name and each injection step by `inject(&lt;place>)`.<br><br>*When* the phase starts, it *shall* start a wall-clock budget of `max(1, floor(timeout_ms / 8))` milliseconds before it encodes the script, and the query *shall* receive what is left of it.<br><br>*When* the phase runs, the report *shall* carry the line `  Bounded witness phase (VER-025):` followed by exactly one of the status lines below.<br><br>*When* a run replays, the phase *shall* return `Violated` with the trimmed run as the counterexample, `counterexampleConfirmed` `true` and the route of the SMT pipeline ([VER-003]), and the result *shall* continue as the witness result of [VER-018] and [VER-019] does.<br><br>*When* the phase returns `Violated` on a net with match transitions, the result *shall* pass the ν guard of [NU-050] as a name-blind verdict and carry the guard's note that the counterexample may be spurious.<br><br>*When* the phase returns `Violated`, the counterexample-timing step of [VER-023] *shall* apply to the result as to every result of the pipeline.<br><br>*If* the solver answers `unsat`, *then* the phase *shall* report that no run of at most `D` steps reaches a violation, and the pipeline *shall* continue to the fixpoint query.<br><br>*If* the query fails in the transport, the solver answers **Assumptions**

- The model is the triple (S, W, P) of ScriptRel, PhaseFn and PipelineFn. S is the script read as a constraint system (P4 of Novel/FiringBound.lean: the SMT-LIB text the ports emit denotes BmcModelEnv, and the solver's sat and unsat are correct). W is the phase from the depth D, the entry gate enter, the name-alignment flag, the flat net as deposit rows (Row = transition and deposit, the exact abstract semantics of VER-004: enabledA, fireAD), the injection list (Inj = flat place index and bound, none under AlwaysAvailable), the seed, the violation isBad and the solver's answer (Witness.Answer: sat with the selector values the model defines, none for a selector it is silent on; unsat; unknown; a transport failure; a spent phase budget). P is the pipeline from the phase outcome, the time spent, the total budget and the fixpoint route as a function of the budget left. The witness triple is ver025_script (BmcModelEnv), witnessPhase and pipeline (Novel/FiringBound/Witness.lean).
- The entry gate of the first three quoted sentences is the input enter: the pipeline reached the flat fixpoint query, the fixpoint query does not take the name-coloured encoding (NU-053), and the net has no match transitions or the property is reachability-safety with a budget place declared. Which nets and properties open it is decided by the pipeline outside the model (VER-001, NU-050), so the sentences are encoded as line 3: the phase runs exactly when enter is true and D is positive. 'Directly before the fixpoint script is encoded' is the order of P: the phase's outcome is decided before the fixpoint route is called (lines 8 to 10).
- The fourth quoted sentence is line 3 at D = 0 and line 10: the phase does not run and the verdict is the fixpoint route's at the whole budget. Its 'route, report and scripts' are not in the model: the route is the fixpoint route's by line 10, the report has no phase line (ver025_report none = [], pinned below), and the scripts of encodeScripts() are outside it.
- The fifth quoted sentence is line 3 and ver025_report none = [] (no report line). 'Send no query' is not expressible: the solver's answer is an input of W, so the model cannot see whether a query was sent; a W that does not run (none) uses no answer. The same holds for 'send no query' in the eighth quoted sentence, whose outcome line 4 fixes for every answer, so the outcome does not depend on one.
- The sixth quoted sentence (Ignore) is the injection list []: under Ignore the verifier builds no injection, and lines 3 to 7 hold at every injection list, [] included, so the phase runs where it runs on any other flat net. At [] the step relation is the firing relation of VER-019 (replayEnv_nil, bmcModelEnv_nil). The Arrivals rewrite produces a closed net, which is again the case injs = [].
- The seventh quoted sentence (the VER-003 replay disabled) is not an input of the model: lines 5 and 6 require the phase's own replay whatever the option, so a run W reports is a replayed one (VER_025_reported_run). counterexampleConfirmed is not in the model; that a run W reports is replayed is VER_025_reported_run.
- The ninth and tenth quoted sentences are about the SMT-LIB text (byte identity across implementations; J = 0 byte-identical to VER-019). The text is not modelled (P4); the scripts are checked by the golden-file parity tests of VER-013. What the model states is the constraint system: lines 1 and 2, and at J = 0 BmcModelEnv is VER-019's BmcModel (bmcModelEnv_nil, cited for VER-025).
- The eleventh quoted sentence (decode) is decodeModel at T + J in lines 5 and 6, and decodeRust in line 2: values in [0, T) are transition steps (rows), values in [T, T + J) injection steps, anything else ends the run, a selector the model leaves undefined (none) is read as idle, and a model that defines none of the selectors below D yields no run, which line 6 makes inconclusive (did not replay), as decode_bounded_run returning None does. Line 2 reads a model of S, which defines every selector (Witness.defined; decodeModel_defined).
- The twelfth quoted sentence (replay) is replays (replayEnv followed by the property) in lines 1, 2, 5 and 6: a transition step fires a row that is enabled (enabledA) and whose successor passes the post-caps (capsOk), an injection step is taken only while its guard holds (injOk: below the bound under Bounded(k), always under AlwaysAvailable) and has no post-cap, and the run is accepted only when every step is taken and the last marking violates (stepIdx, Bmc.lean). That this is the step relation of the HORN rules is stepEnv_injsOf (StepEnv at the verifier's injection list is EnvSemantics.StepAE), cited for VER-025; that a replayed run is a derivation in the strengthened CHC system is witness_horn_derivation.
- The thirteenth quoted sentence (trim) is line 5: the reported run is trim of the decoded run, the reference trim of Witness.lean (violatingPrefix: the shortest prefix that replays to a violating marking, the empty one included; then passes from the last index to the first, each replacing the run by the violating prefix of the run without that step when one exists, repeated until a pass changes nothing). The algorithm is part of the statement, so the run is fixed for a model and a trim in another order is told apart (VER_025_forbids_trimFirst), as is one without the cut (VER_025_forbids_noCut). What follows, from the statement alone (VER_025_reported_run, VER_025_initial_violation): the reported run is a sublist of the decoded run, replays, ends at the first violating marking it reaches, has no single step that can be dropped, and is the empty run when M0 violates. The trimmed run is not claimed to be a shortest run.
- The fourteenth and seventeenth quoted sentences are line 5 (the reported run is the trimmed run, replayed) and line 8 (the result is Violated with that run). The labels (a transition's name, inject(<place>)) are the pure function ver025_stepLabel, pinned below. counterexampleConfirmed true, the route of the SMT pipeline and the result text of VER-018 and VER-019 (RESULT, VIOLATED, the trace, the Firing sequence line, the untimed warning) are outside the model.
- The fifteenth quoted sentence (budget) is the pure function ver025_budgetMs, pinned below. The wall clock, the transport's clamp and 'the query shall receive what is left of it' are not modelled: elapsed is any number the phase spent, line 9 charges it against the total budget, and a spent phase budget is the answer budgetSpent (line 7).
- The sixteenth quoted sentence and the status lines are the pure functions ver025_header, ver025_status and ver025_report, pinned below: ver025_report gives no line when the phase does not run and the header and exactly one status line when it does. The reasons are ver025_reasonText; the transport's failure message (a reply with an (error ...) line included, which is the answer failure) and the NU-055 reason are parameters, since the spec does not fix their text in VER-025.
- The eighteenth quoted sentence (the ν guard of NU-050) and the nineteenth (the counterexample-timing step of VER-023) are steps the result passes through after the pipeline of this model; neither is modelled. The model's Violated is the phase's result before them.
- The twentieth to twenty-third quoted sentences are lines 6, 7, 9 and 10: unsat gives 'no run' and every other ending without a run gives inconclusive with its reason (lines 6, 7), and the pipeline then hands over to the fixpoint route at the total budget minus the time the phase spent (line 9), so the phase changes no verdict except through that time. The pipeline answers Proven only through the fixpoint route (VER_025_never_proven, from lines 8 to 10; Witness.Outcome has no proven outcome at all). 'Shall not read an unsat answer as a proof' is lines 7 and 9 together: unsat gives 'no run', after which the verdict is the fixpoint route's (VER_025_forbids_unsatProven). What 'no run' means is line 1 under P4: no run of at most D steps reaches a violation (VER_025_noRun_exact below, from the statement). It says nothing about D + 1 steps.
- The twenty-fourth and twenty-sixth quoted sentences (default 8, the negative-depth error) are the pure functions ver025_depthDefault and ver025_depthError, pinned below. The twenty-fifth (a positive n asks one query at depth n) is the depth argument D of W, at which lines 5 and 6 decode; that one query is sent is not modelled, as for 'send no query'.
- The twenty-seventh quoted sentence (the dump phase name witness) is the constant ver025_dumpPhase, pinned below; the dump itself is not modelled. The twenty-eighth (encodeScripts' witness member) is about the scripts, which are not modelled (P4).
- AC1 (envBoundedPair: t takes one(e) to p1, e under Bounded(2), empty M0, PlaceBound(p1, 1)) is VER_025_nonvacuous: at depth 8, a padded model's run of 5 steps is trimmed to a run of 4 steps, two inject(e) and two t, that replays and is irredundant, its status line is 'a run of 4 steps reaches a violation (replayed; depth 8)', and the pipeline answers Violated without the fixpoint route (no fixpoint query). 'Confirmed' is outside the model (seventh quoted sentence).
- AC2 (the same net, PlaceBound(p1, 4), shortest run 10 steps) is VER_025_ac2: at depth 10 a model gives a reported run of 10 steps; at depth 8 the answer unsat gives 'no run' (line 7), its status line is pinned, and the pipeline then answers what the fixpoint route answers at the budget left (line 9). That the depth-8 script is in fact unsat is the solver's answer under P4 (line 1 says what it means); it is not re-derived here by enumerating runs.
- AC3 (depth 0 off) is line 3 and line 10, and ver025_report none = []; the encoded scripts and the dump are outside the model.
- AC4 (the name-coloured encoding) and AC5 (the ν gates) are the entry gate enter of line 3, which the pipeline sets outside the model. AC5's ν guard note is the eighteenth quoted sentence, not modelled.
- AC6 (name alignment) is line 4.
- AC7 (the stub replies unsat, unknown, a transport failure, a spent budget, a sat model whose run does not replay: each its own status line, then the fixpoint query, never Proven) is lines 6, 7 and 9, VER_025_never_proven and the status lines pinned below.
- AC8 (selector range: T + j decodes as injection j, T + J or more or a negative selector ends the run) is decodeRust and decodeModel in lines 2, 5 and 6, pinned on examples below (VER_025_ac8), with an undefined selector read as idle and a model with no selector read as no run.
- AC9 (injection replay: an injection at a place holding its bound does not replay, an unbounded one always does, its label is inject(<place>), no post-cap) is the reference replay of lines 5 and 6, pinned on examples below (VER_025_ac9), and ver025_stepLabel.
- AC10 (trim: a padded model is reported as a run of 4 steps; dropping any single step of a reported run makes it fail to replay) is line 5 with VER_025_reported_run, and VER_025_nonvacuous.
- AC11 (M0 violates: a run of 0 steps) is VER_025_initial_violation (from the statement: a reported run is [] whenever M0 violates, whatever model the solver returned) and VER_025_ac11: an all-idle model, and a model on the ring t1: p0 to p1, t2: p1 to p0 that leaves M0 and comes back to a violating marking, are both reported as the run []; a run that passes a violating marking and goes on is reported cut there; its status line is 'a run of 0 steps'. The enumeration route and VER-018/019 being off is the entry gate.
- AC12 (the replay option off) is the seventh quoted sentence: lines 5 and 6 hold whatever the option.
- AC13 (Ignore) is the sixth quoted sentence: the injection list is [].
- AC14 (scripts: J = 0 byte-identical to VER-019, golden witness.smt2, dump file names) is about the SMT-LIB text and the dump, outside the model (P4); at the constraint level, J = 0 is bmcModelEnv_nil.
- AC15 (default 8, one query at a positive n, the error for -1) is ver025_depthDefault and ver025_depthError, pinned below, and the depth argument of W.
- The test derivation (the envBoundedPair fixtures at depths 8 and 10, one test per gate and outcome, the depth-0 opt-out of tests that pin the fixpoint query) is AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC7, as above.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): The reference triple satisfies VER-025: the script is exact (`bmcEnv_complete`), a model's decoded run replays (`bmcEnv_sat_replays`), a reported run is the trim of a `sat` model's decoded run (`witnessPhase_violated_sound`), the outcomes are those of `witnessPhase`'s cases, and the pipeline hands every outcome but a run to the fixpoint route at the total budget minus the time the phase spent (`pipeline_some_eq`).
  <pre>VER_025 ver025_script Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_alwaysSat` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A script that is always satisfiable violates VER-025 (line 1): on the empty net with a violation no marking satisfies, it has a model although no run reaches a violation.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_alwaysSat Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_depth0Runs` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A phase that still runs at depth 0 violates VER-025 (line 3): at depth 0 with the gate open it reports 'no run' on `unsat` instead of not running.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script ver025_depth0Runs Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_dropLast` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A trim that drops a needed step violates VER-025 (line 5): the run `inject(e) inject(e) t t` is reported without its last `t`, which is not the trimmed run.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script ver025_dropLast Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_emptyModelRun` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A phase that reads a run from a model with no selector violates VER-025 (line 6): when `M0` violates, it reports the run of 0 steps from a model that defines nothing.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script ver025_emptyModelRun Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_noBound` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ An injection step that ignores its bound violates VER-025 (line 6): three injections into `e` under `Bounded(2)` are reported as a run to `e = 3`, which the exact step relation refuses at the third injection.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script ver025_noBound Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_noCut` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A trim without the cut to the violating prefix violates VER-025 (line 5): on the ring with `M0` violating, the model `t1, t2` comes back to a violating marking, no single step of it can be dropped, and it is reported as a run of 2 steps instead of the run of 0 steps.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script (ver025_phaseWith Novel.FiringBound.decodeModel ver025_noCut)<br>    Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_noDeduct` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A pipeline that ignores the time the phase spent violates VER-025 (line 9): the phase's time counts against the total budget.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase ver025_noDeduct</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_noReplay` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A phase that does not replay violates VER-025 (line 6): a model selecting `t` first on `envBoundedPair` decodes to the run `t`, which is not a run (`e` is empty), and the phase reports it.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script ver025_noReplay Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_starve` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A pipeline that starves the fixpoint route violates VER-025 (line 9): 'no run' after 1 ms of an 8 ms budget turns a fixpoint `Proven` at the 7 ms left into `Unknown`. A statement that only bounds the budget left by the total would accept it.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase ver025_starve</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_trimFirst` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A trim in another order violates VER-025 (line 5), although its run replays, ends at its first violating marking and is irredundant: from the model `inject(0) inject(1)` it reports `inject(1)`, where the reference cuts the run to `inject(0)`. The quoted trim fixes the run for a model, so the ports report the same run.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script (ver025_phaseWith Novel.FiringBound.decodeModel ver025_trimFirst)<br>    Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_unsatProven` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A pipeline that answers `Proven` on the phase's `unsat` violates VER-025 (line 9): with a fixpoint route that answers `Unknown`, it answers `Proven`.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase ver025_unsatProven</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✓ **AC1 and AC10**: on `envBoundedPair` with `PlaceBound(p1, 1)` at depth 8, a model padded with a needless injection (`inject(e) t inject(e) inject(e) t`, then idle) is reported as the run `inject(e) t inject(e) t`: four steps, two of them injections, that replay to `p1 = 2`; dropping any single step leaves a run that does not replay to a violation (so the run needs both injections); and the pipeline answers `Violated` with that run whatever the fixpoint route would have answered (no fixpoint query).
  <pre>Novel.FiringBound.decodeModel 2 (ver025_model [1, 0, 1, 1, 0]) 8 = some [1, 0, 1, 1, 0] ∧<br>  Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase 8 true false ver025_rows ver025_injs ver025_a0<br>        (ver025_placeBound 1)<br>        (Novel.FiringBound.Witness.Answer.sat (ver025_model [1, 0, 1, 1, 0])) =<br>      some (Novel.FiringBound.Witness.Outcome.violated [1, 0, 1, 0]) ∧<br>    List.count 1 [1, 0, 1, 0] = 2 ∧<br>      Novel.FiringBound.replays ver025_rows ver025_injs (ver025_placeBound 1) ver025_a0<br>            [1, 0, 1, 0] =<br>          true ∧<br>        (∀ k &lt; 4,<br>            Novel.FiringBound.replays ver025_rows ver025_injs (ver025_placeBound 1)<br>                ver025_a0 ([1, 0, 1, 0].eraseIdx k) =<br>              false) ∧<br>          (Novel.FiringBound.pipeline<br>              (Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase 8 true false ver025_rows ver025_injs<br>                ver025_a0 (ver025_placeBound 1)<br>                (Novel.FiringBound.Witness.Answer.sat (ver025_model [1, 0, 1, 1, 0])))<br>              1 8 fun x ↦ Novel.FiringBound.Witness.Verdict.unknown) =<br>            Novel.FiringBound.Witness.Verdict.violated [1, 0, 1, 0]</pre>
- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_consistent` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✓ VER-025 is consistent: the reference script, phase and pipeline satisfy it. Its model (a script, a phase and a pipeline) shares no component with the firing relations of the CORE, IO, EXEC and TIME blocks, so it has its own consistency theorem rather than a conjunct of theirs.
  <pre>∃ S W P, VER_025 S W P</pre>
